issue: Unexpected behaviour in the media transcoder across the primary cluster.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the media transcoder did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Resolution for the document indexer failed intermittently for 24% of clients, and the first remediation attempt made it worse. Impact was limited to the primary region.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the document indexer still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Every service that resolved the affected name failed together, which made the blast radius far larger than the change implied.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: The web dashboard slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Instances of the export worker in the primary region were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the export worker at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The web dashboard displayed incorrect values to 42% of users for 6 hours 10 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A rounding change in the token validator was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Background jobs in the billing service stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of eight thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the invoices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the metrics agent rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the metrics agent to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Callers of the webhook dispatcher saw response times multiply for 1 hour 47 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The config loader began synchronously calling the cloud provider block-storage service on a path that had previously been asynchronous. Each request inherited the dependency latency, and the thread pool filled with waiting work.
solution: Moved the call to the cloud provider block-storage service back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the notification service made the incident worse and extended impact by 38 minutes.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the object store bucket, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the object store bucket, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the reporting API. The new default disagreed with the token validator, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the token validator cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The asset pipeline could not create new records, returning a database-level error unrelated to any application change. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the sessions table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted.

issue: The admin console became slow for a small subset of users while backend services reported normal replication lag.
root_cause: A client-side change in the admin console issued one request per item rather than a single batched call. Each individual request was fast, so backend metrics stayed normal while the aggregate page load grew to several seconds.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: Routing for the checkout service sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting 31% of traffic. Both the CLI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the checkout service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path.

issue: New deployments of the messaging bridge hung in a pending state for 23 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the messaging bridge did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the pricing engine did not set, so the token validator silently rejected every new instance. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the token validator to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the search API in production.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the search API stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the search API actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: 42% of test runs against the messaging bridge failed unpredictably after a performance change. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A rewrite of the input handling in the leader elector introduced a low-level synchronisation path with an incorrect ordering assumption.
solution: Corrected the synchronisation ordering in the rewritten path and added a stress test that runs the affected code under deliberately adverse timing.

issue: A low-risk change to production resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving production was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Traffic to the entitlement service failing to reach its destination. Impact was limited to two of three availability zones.
root_cause: A script restarted only the authoritative resolver after an address change and left the caching resolver untouched, so cached lookups began timing out. The subsequent repair rebuilt the zone using a tool that itself depended on working DNS, producing a zone that returned not-found for many names. The change looked routine in review because its effect depended on which resolver path a caller happened to use.
solution: Rebuilt and republished a correct zone by hand, restarted both resolvers, and added a rule that DNS-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a DNS outage.

issue: Just under half of payment attempts on the mobile apps timed out for 1 hour 47 minutes during a demand surge.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the webhook dispatcher to a third-party email provider became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts.

issue: 18% of requests to the embedded widget were served by an unintended backend for 38 minutes. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the billing service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Processing in the webhook dispatcher did not complete as expected. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the webhook dispatcher placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. A cached fallback and status indicator were added so an upstream fault degrades the feature rather than removing it.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the public API.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced a regional fault. The billing service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the sync service in eu-west.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service began returning errors for a subset of requests. The serialisation layer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the cloud provider block-storage service.

issue: The search API unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the search API was raised past what any node in two of three availability zones could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The config loader had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the config loader to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: The embedded widget began returning errors for just under half of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the media transcoder itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the media transcoder. The new default disagreed with the cache layer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the cache layer cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: Nodes running the sync service restarted repeatedly on out-of-memory conditions, and cluster leadership moved between them.
root_cause: A background agent on each node retried a failing call to the managed Kubernetes control plane in a loop, retaining the context of every attempt. Under sustained load the retained contexts exhausted available memory and the node was terminated.
solution: Bounded the retry loop and released the context between attempts, then added alerting specific to this agent's memory use since the node's normal dynamic usage had masked the growth. A bound was placed on the retained structure so its size no longer tracks process lifetime.

issue: A small subset of API clients received throttling responses from the entitlement service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the metrics agent identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. As queues grew, client retries added load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the metrics agent so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the reporting UI.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the cache layer uses to validate credentials for the catalogue API.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect.

issue: The billing service became slow in us-west only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in us-west left the billing service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Restored the instance count in us-west and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: The messaging bridge could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-southeast.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the messaging bridge did not set, so the request router silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the request router to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: 31% of requests to the media transcoder failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure. Both the public API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider experienced an outage in the Sydney region. The media transcoder called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed DNS provider recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Requests to the pricing engine failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the pricing engine started with settings it could not validate. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the pricing engine within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to all regions.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the billing service started with settings it could not validate. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the billing service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: New deployments of the recommendation service hung in a pending state for 14 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the recommendation service did not set, so the request router silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the request router to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Requests to the inventory service queued and timed out while the Cassandra ring itself remained lightly loaded. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The connection pool for the inventory service was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the Cassandra ring would accept and new connections were refused. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the audit log writer.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the request router made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Alerting was keyed on error rate rather than on completion rate, so a silent stall produced no signal.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the request router to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the messaging bridge started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the messaging bridge within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 51 minutes, while the payments themselves completed normally.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the job scheduler made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Because the money movement itself was unaffected, internal dashboards showed success while customers saw failure.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the job scheduler to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries. A deadline was introduced so a payment attempt fails fast instead of consuming capacity it cannot use.

issue: API tokens for the notification service were rejected as invalid for 38 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the Redis cache tier did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the admission controller could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the Redis cache tier and changed the admission controller to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The webhook dispatcher stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the devices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the health checker rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the health checker to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Lower-priority processing in eu-west was delayed by 14 minutes during planned maintenance.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Payment failures affecting the SDK.
root_cause: The search API could not scale out to meet the surge because its resource configuration prevented new instances from being placed, even though spare capacity existed.
solution: Corrected the resource configuration so instances could be scheduled onto available capacity, and added load testing ahead of promotional events to surface scaling limits in advance.

issue: New deployments of the media transcoder hung in a pending state for 1 hour 47 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the media transcoder did not set, so the metrics agent silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the metrics agent to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Payment failures affecting the partner API.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the leader elector made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Downstream ledger entries were written from the same flow, so the inconsistency propagated into reporting.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the leader elector to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries. Idempotency keys are now required on every call to the processor so a retry cannot create a second payment.

issue: The asset pipeline unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the asset pipeline was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: 24% of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the audit log writer and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: The reporting API stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 9 hours.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the entitlements table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the sidecar proxy rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the sidecar proxy to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Data access failures in a single production cell.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the audit table. solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the cache layer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: A traffic spike on the embedded widget pushed the asset pipeline past its capacity and roughly a third of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the asset pipeline had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete. Queues grew past the per-tenant quota and requests began failing after already consuming capacity.
solution: Added admission control so the asset pipeline rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: The document indexer unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the document indexer did not set, so the shard mapper silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the shard mapper to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: A feature intended for internal testing became active for 55% of customers on the reporting UI without an announcement. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A feature flag for the catalogue API was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The webhook dispatcher shedding requests under load.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the webhook dispatcher had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete. Queues grew past the configured memory ceiling and requests began failing after already consuming capacity.
solution: Added admission control so the webhook dispatcher rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Users reported the search API being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: The partner API began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. The affected path had no concurrency limit, so a single slow dependency was enough to occupy every available worker.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time.

issue: Queries against the devices table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the reporting API began timing out for 78% of requests.
root_cause: A new query against the devices table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the primary Postgres cluster. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the pricing engine, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the pricing engine failed to reconnect after a restart of the retry handler and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Payment records inconsistent for a subset of customers.
root_cause: A failover of the Elasticsearch index mid-transaction left a partial record. The reconciliation job treated the partial row as missing and re-submitted it, producing a duplicate. Alerting was keyed on error rate rather than on completion rate, so a silent stall produced no signal.
solution: Reversed the duplicates, and changed reconciliation to resolve a partial record against the processor's ledger before re-submitting anything.

issue: Memory use by the notification service climbed steadily under sustained load until the process was terminated and restarted.
root_cause: The rate limiter registered a listener for each request but never removed it, so the registry grew for the lifetime of the process. Every entry remained reachable, which is why heap analysis showed no conventional leak.
solution: Removed the listener when a request completes and added a bound on the registry size, after which memory stabilised under sustained load.

issue: The majority of payment attempts on the partner API timed out for most of the working day during a demand surge.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the document indexer to a partner inventory feed became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts.

issue: The ingest gateway could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-central.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the ingest gateway did not set, so the leader elector silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the leader elector to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Errors on the admin console following a recent change.
root_cause: A feature flag for the entitlement service was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Federated login to the ingest gateway broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the queue consumer caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the queue consumer, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: The identity service degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The request router had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the request router so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: The majority of requests to the messaging bridge were rejected at the edge while the service itself reported healthy.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the messaging bridge, and the rule applied to a single production cell rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The billing service became unavailable in ap-southeast following a disk failure on a node that continued reporting itself healthy.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the billing service failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the inventory service across production.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the object store bucket, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the object store bucket, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The entitlement service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in the primary region. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the entitlement service did not set, so the rate limiter silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the rate limiter to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the media transcoder did not restore service and left the Kafka topic in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Kafka topic, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Kafka topic, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to a single production cell.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the entitlement service.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the cache layer cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: A traffic spike on the webhooks endpoint pushed the inventory service past its capacity and 42% of requests failed.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the inventory service for every caller. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was degraded for 3 hours 20 minutes because of a fault at a third-party email provider rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The cache layer had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Added response validation in the cache layer so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: 24% of requests to the admin console failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The health checker had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Added response validation in the health checker so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: A subset of transactions in the inventory service were recorded twice over a most of the working day window.
root_cause: A retry in the serialisation layer re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost. Without an idempotency key, an upstream payment processor treated the retry as a new transaction. The failure occurred after authorisation but before confirmation, which left records in an ambiguous state.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to an upstream payment processor so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: Calls to the recommendation service were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 42% of clients.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the token validator identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the token validator so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Payouts from the sync service were delayed by 6 hours 10 minutes for 11% of recipients.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the queue consumer rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the queue consumer to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: The shared staging-to-production path lost external connectivity for 4 hours 36 minutes, including the remote access paths needed to diagnose the problem.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the media transcoder was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: New deployments of the identity service hung in a pending state for 14 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the identity service did not set, so the job scheduler silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the job scheduler to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Read and write errors against the primary Postgres cluster.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the sessions table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the queue consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the queue consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: A small subset of requests to the admin console failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The token validator had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Added response validation in the token validator so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to all regions.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the health checker but the sync service reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the search API responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the cache layer expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The ingest gateway degraded by a datastore problem. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the object store bucket.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Just under half of requests to the public API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The health checker had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Added response validation in the health checker so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The reporting API was degraded for 1 hour 12 minutes because of a fault at an external geolocation API rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced a regional fault. The reporting API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the webhooks endpoint.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the catalogue API was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the ingest gateway stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the ingest gateway actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The webhooks endpoint displayed incorrect values to 18% of users for 14 minutes while every service reported healthy. Impact was limited to the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the chat backend placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: The messaging bridge stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the devices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the queue consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the queue consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The media transcoder failed to start in ap-southeast after a dependency upgrade, and just under half of requests to the mobile apps returned errors.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the admission controller still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the shared staging-to-production path. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Errors on the public API following a recent change. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the catalogue API was raised past what any node in the Sydney region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the retry handler to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: 7% of API clients received throttling responses from the ingest gateway despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the request router identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.

Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: API tokens for the asset pipeline were rejected as invalid for 1 hour 47 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the connection pool was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the primary cluster. Both the mobile apps and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the ingest gateway was raised past what any node in the primary region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region.

issue: Garbage-collection pause time on the pricing engine rose from normal to several seconds, and 78% of calls to the public API exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: The serialisation layer began synchronously calling a third-party email provider on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to a third-party email provider back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: Elevated response times on the partner API. Both the partner API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: Instances of the billing service in ap-southeast were routed to the SQLite metadata store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the billing service at the local replica of the SQLite metadata store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the config loader still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in a single production cell. issue: Requests to the geocoding service failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the geocoding service. The new default disagreed with the cache layer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the cache layer cannot parse before it reaches production.

issue: The mobile apps slow or unresponsive. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in eu-west left the identity service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in eu-west and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the webhook dispatcher made the incident worse and extended impact by most of the working day. Impact was limited to two of three availability zones.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the SQLite metadata store, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the SQLite metadata store, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in us-west.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the cache layer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the cache layer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: The admin console began returning errors for 24% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the billing service itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the billing service. The new default disagreed with the token validator, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the token validator cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: Requests to the checkout service failed across a single production cell immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the checkout service started with settings it could not validate. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the checkout service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The webhook dispatcher became unavailable in two of three availability zones following a disk failure on a node that continued reporting itself healthy.
root_cause: A node in two of three availability zones entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations. The probe tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the scheduling service.
root_cause: Instances of the scheduling service in ap-northeast were routed to the Redis cache tier in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the scheduling service at the local replica of the Redis cache tier and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The public API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the queue consumer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. As queues grew, client retries added load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the queue consumer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: 55% of requests from the geocoding service were sent to instances that no longer existed. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the geocoding service failed to reconnect after a restart of the config loader and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Federated login to the feed builder broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the connection pool. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period.

issue: 18% of API clients received throttling responses from the export worker despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the shard mapper treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing.

issue: Payment failures affecting the web dashboard.
root_cause: A change to the queue infrastructure behind the media transcoder caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection without raising an error. Callbacks queued for those workers were never delivered and the absence of errors was read as healthy. Reconciliation ran only daily, so the discrepancy was not surfaced until well after the window closed.
solution: Replayed the undelivered callbacks once identified, then added active health checks on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors. Idempotency keys are now required on every call to the processor so a retry cannot create a second payment.

issue: The recommendation service degraded for a subset of users. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The recommendation service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The public API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in ap-southeast were routed to the DynamoDB table in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the DynamoDB table and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: A scheduled job in the audit log writer did not run for 2 hours 5 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the Redis cache tier was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the audit log writer.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the DynamoDB table did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the config loader could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. Service-to-service calls used the same validation path, so internal workflows failed alongside end-user sign-in.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the DynamoDB table and changed the config loader to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. A pre-apply check now lists every resource a policy change will affect before it is applied.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the ingest gateway in the production fleet.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the ingest gateway stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the ingest gateway actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: 94% of requests to the embedded widget were served by an unintended backend for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the catalogue API were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: Requests to the CLI failed TLS negotiation for just under half of clients starting at a fixed time of day.

Negative results were cached downstream, so the failure persisted for some clients after the underlying record was corrected.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Capacity in ap-southeast fell by 7% and the identity service began shedding requests.

Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down.
