issue: API tokens for the reporting API were rejected as invalid for 51 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the leader elector was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the ClickHouse cluster in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the billing service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Healthy instances of the document indexer were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 3 hours 20 minutes window.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time.

issue: Request throughput on the chat backend rose from normal to several seconds, and 18% of calls to the mobile apps exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the chat backend.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the audit log writer unable to serve traffic in a single production cell.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The retry handler had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the retry handler to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Elevated query latency against the MySQL replica set. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A query plan on the subscriptions table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the billing service in the Sydney region.
root_cause: A node in the Sydney region entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone.

issue: The asset pipeline degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the queue consumer but the asset pipeline reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete.

issue: The chat backend stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the invoices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the config loader rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the config loader to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The checkout service unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the checkout service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock.

issue: The asset pipeline degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the asset pipeline did not set, so the request router silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the request router to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Requests to the search API failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the search API started with settings it could not validate. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the search API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The recommendation service failed to start in the primary region after a dependency upgrade, and 94% of requests to the public API returned errors.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the shard mapper still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in production.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The entitlement service was offline for 6 hours 10 minutes after a power event at the facility hosting all regions.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting all regions was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events.

issue: The messaging bridge shedding requests under load. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A cache in front of the time-series store was configured with an expiry short enough that most reads missed.
solution: Lengthened the cache expiry to a value matched to how often the underlying data actually changes, which raised the hit rate and returned latency to normal.

issue: Reports generated by the catalogue API contained figures that did not reconcile with the underlying records.
root_cause: A rounding change in the batch consumer was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the checkout service. The new default disagreed with the batch consumer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the batch consumer cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: The majority of requests to the admin console were served by an unintended backend for most of the working day.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the media transcoder were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: The web dashboard began returning errors for 31% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the notification service itself. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the notification service started with settings it could not validate. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the notification service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Traffic to the asset pipeline failing to reach its destination.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the asset pipeline still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the SDK.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the Redis cache tier did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the job scheduler could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the Redis cache tier and changed the job scheduler to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: The geocoding service timing out for a subset of callers. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: Instances of the geocoding service in the primary region were routed to the DynamoDB table in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the geocoding service at the local replica of the DynamoDB table and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Checkout on the SDK failed for the majority of attempts during a promotional traffic peak. Impact was limited to the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the document indexer to the cloud provider block-storage service became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts. Idempotency keys are now required on every call to the processor so a retry cannot create a second payment.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the notification service made the incident worse and extended impact by 9 hours.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the object store bucket, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the object store bucket, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Requests to the export worker failed across the primary cluster immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the export worker. The new default disagreed with the job scheduler, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the job scheduler cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: The inventory service unavailable following a planned change. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the inventory service. The new default disagreed with the shard mapper, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the shard mapper cannot parse before it reaches production.

issue: The partner API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: The retry handler began synchronously calling an external geolocation API on a path that had previously been asynchronous. Each request inherited the dependency latency, and the thread pool filled with waiting work.
solution: Moved the call to an external geolocation API back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Resolution for the pricing engine failed intermittently for 18% of clients, and the first remediation attempt made it worse.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the pricing engine still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: The sync service slowed progressively over 14 minutes, with connection count degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache in front of the Redis cache tier was configured with an expiry short enough that most reads missed. Each miss fell through to the Redis cache tier, so the cache added overhead without absorbing load. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Lengthened the cache expiry to a value matched to how often the underlying data actually changes, which raised the hit rate and returned latency to normal.

issue: The inventory service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the subscriptions table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the leader elector rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the leader elector to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The chat backend stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 4 hours 36 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the audit table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the connection pool rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the connection pool to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The public API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: A cache key for the checkout service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the Cassandra ring.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: Elevated query latency against the SQLite metadata store.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the connection pool selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: The geocoding service degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 7% of queries exceeded their timeout. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: A query plan on the sessions table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the audit log writer.
root_cause: A third-party email provider experienced a regional fault. The audit log writer depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party email provider recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A scheduled job in the entitlement service did not run for 51 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the entitlement service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: New deployments of the checkout service hung in a pending state for 1 hour 47 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the checkout service was raised past what any node in the Sydney region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Users were unable to sign in or load the public API platform-wide, with error rates climbing for 2 hours 5 minutes.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the primary Postgres cluster past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The ClickHouse cluster became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the ClickHouse cluster.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Requests to the feed builder failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the feed builder. The new default disagreed with the cache layer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the cache layer cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: Database errors affecting the messaging bridge.
root_cause: A query plan on the orders table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Batch workloads on the inventory service ran at reduced throughput for 51 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: A feature intended for internal testing became active for 85% of customers on the admin console without an announcement.
root_cause: A targeting rule meant to match a single internal tenant used a prefix comparison, so it matched a large set of production tenant identifiers that shared the same prefix.
solution: Corrected the targeting rule to an exact-match comparison and added a dry-run report that lists which tenants a rule will match before it is saved.

issue: The web dashboard displayed incorrect values to 55% of users for 14 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A rounding change in the health checker was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: 94% of requests to the public API failed while every internal component reported healthy. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The retry handler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Because every internal component reported healthy, responders spent much of the incident ruling out their own systems.
solution: Added response validation in the retry handler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The checkout service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in us-east.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the checkout service was raised past what any node in us-east could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: A power interruption took a single production cell offline and recovery took considerably longer than planned.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the audit log writer were found to share an upstream component. When that component failed, both feeds dropped together despite the design being described as redundant.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to a single production cell.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The batch consumer had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the batch consumer to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Data access failures in a single production cell.
root_cause: An index on the subscriptions table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the object store bucket. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The reporting API was degraded for 51 minutes because of a fault at the managed Kubernetes control plane rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced a regional fault. The reporting API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Intermittent connection failures in ap-northeast.
root_cause: A static routing configuration had not kept pace with infrastructure growth, so updated discovery information could not reach every consumer. Clients continued working from a stale view and sent traffic to instances that had been replaced. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Restored discovery data to the affected consumers and changed the routing configuration to scale with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: A handful of requests to the search API failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced an outage in the Frankfurt region. The search API called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Processing in the recommendation service did not complete as expected.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the Elasticsearch index was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: The catalogue API was degraded for 4 hours 36 minutes because of an outage at the managed DNS provider.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider experienced an outage in eu-west. The catalogue API called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed DNS provider recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Just under half of requests to the media transcoder failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service began returning errors for a subset of requests. The batch consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the cloud provider block-storage service.

issue: The export worker silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the audit table without updates.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the Cassandra ring was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the messaging bridge.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the messaging bridge placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Errors on the webhooks endpoint following a recent change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the search API did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the webhooks endpoint was blocked for 38 minutes with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the geocoding service, and the rule applied to a single production cell rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The feed builder silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the entitlements table without updates.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the feed builder was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in sa-east below what was needed to serve normal traffic.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: Database errors affecting the feed builder. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the time-series store.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: 31% of API clients received throttling responses from the media transcoder despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the metrics agent treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: A handful of requests from the ingest gateway were sent to instances that no longer existed.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the ingest gateway failed to reconnect after a restart of the admission controller and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age.

issue: New deployments of the inventory service hung in a pending state for 1 hour 47 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the inventory service was raised past what any node in ap-northeast could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The recommendation service was unavailable for 3 hours 20 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.

Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the audit log writer in sa-east.
root_cause: A node in sa-east entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: Requests to the entitlement service failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the entitlement service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the entitlement service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Callers of the reporting API saw response times multiply for 14 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the reporting API.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client.

issue: The notification service degraded for a subset of users. Both the public API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: An external geolocation API began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The shard mapper had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the shard mapper so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The inventory service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in sa-east. Both the embedded widget and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the inventory service did not set, so the config loader silently rejected every new instance. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Latency on the ingest gateway was 55% higher in one region for most of the working day with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in ap-northeast were routed to the Cassandra ring in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the Cassandra ring and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The catalogue API degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and garbage-collection pause time on the MySQL replica set rose steadily for 1 hour 47 minutes.
root_cause: A new query against the accounts table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the MySQL replica set. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The search API degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: The upstream CDN experienced a regional fault. The search API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the upstream CDN recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Just under half of requests to the webhooks endpoint failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced a regional fault. The catalogue API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The geocoding service was degraded for 6 hours 10 minutes because of a fault at a third-party SMS gateway rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced a regional fault. The geocoding service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: 7% of legitimate requests to the web dashboard were dropped during a sustained attack.
root_cause: An attack targeted an endpoint on the ingest gateway whose responses were expensive to generate and not cached, so a modest request rate was enough to exhaust backend capacity.
solution: Added caching and a strict rate limit to the expensive endpoint, and placed it behind authentication so it cannot be reached anonymously at volume.

issue: The catalogue API degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and the majority of queries exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: A query plan on the webhooks table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again.

issue: The document indexer degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the document indexer did not set, so the request router silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the request router to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the inventory service did not restore service and left the MongoDB shard in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the MongoDB shard, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the MongoDB shard, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Latency on the messaging bridge was 42% higher in one region for 51 minutes with no configuration difference. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in us-east left the messaging bridge running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in us-east and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: 78% of API clients received throttling responses from the audit log writer despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the shard mapper identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the shard mapper so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the webhooks endpoint was blocked for most of the working day with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A filtering rule was changed directly on the edge tier outside the normal pipeline, so the change did not appear in deployment history. Responders spent most of the incident examining recent releases before drift detection surfaced the untracked edit.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band edge change and restricted write access so edits outside the pipeline are blocked, with drift detection alerting on any that still occur.

issue: The billing service degraded by a platform-level failure.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced an outage in sa-east. The billing service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Resolution for the recommendation service failed intermittently for 24% of clients, and the first remediation attempt made it worse.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the recommendation service still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake.

issue: Security incident affecting the export worker.
root_cause: A distributed attack saturated the edge capacity serving the mobile apps. Mitigation rules existed but were scoped to a traffic profile the attack did not match, so they did not engage automatically. Audit logging covered the application but not the administrative path that was used, which complicated scoping.
solution: Applied mitigation manually to absorb the attack, then broadened the automatic rules to cover this traffic profile and raised edge capacity headroom.

issue: The messaging bridge shedding requests under load. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: Instances of the messaging bridge in the Sydney region were routed to the object store bucket in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the messaging bridge at the local replica of the object store bucket and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The media transcoder became slow in ap-southeast only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in ap-southeast left the media transcoder running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in ap-southeast and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: New deployments of the feed builder hung in a pending state for 9 hours, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the feed builder was raised past what any node in two of three availability zones could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Callers of the asset pipeline saw response times multiply for 38 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the asset pipeline. As requests queued, client retries added further load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the billing service in production.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the billing service stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the billing service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The reporting UI began returning errors for 42% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the sync service itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the sync service started with settings it could not validate. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the sync service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Infrastructure fault degrading the document indexer.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the document indexer, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only. The redundancy that was expected to cover this failure shared an upstream component with the path that failed.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: The CLI began returning errors for roughly a third of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the export worker itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the export worker. The new default disagreed with the batch consumer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the batch consumer cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was degraded for most of the working day because of a fault at a third-party email provider rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The sidecar proxy had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the sidecar proxy so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: A migration on the ledger table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the ledger table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the web dashboard. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the job scheduler caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the job scheduler, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the embedded widget. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the catalogue API placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records.

issue: Requests to the export worker queued and timed out while the object store bucket itself remained lightly loaded. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: The connection pool for the export worker was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the object store bucket would accept and new connections were refused. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The identity service was degraded for 9 hours because of an outage at a third-party SMS gateway.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced an outage in ap-southeast. The identity service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The entitlement service was degraded for 23 minutes because of an outage at an external geolocation API. Both the embedded widget and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced an outage in eu-west. The entitlement service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Served a degraded response while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: A low-risk change to all regions resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving all regions was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The Cassandra ring became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the Cassandra ring.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: A small subset of test runs against the ingest gateway failed unpredictably after a performance change.
root_cause: Shared state in the session store was accessed without synchronisation from a callback that could run on a different thread, so corruption appeared only when the callback overlapped with a request.
solution: Confined the shared state behind a single owner and added a race detector to the test pipeline so this class of defect fails the build. Fencing tokens were introduced so writes from a superseded leader are rejected.

issue: The feed builder degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 85% of queries exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: An index on the ledger table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the primary Postgres cluster.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: The export worker was degraded for most of the working day because of an outage at a third-party email provider.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning errors for a subset of requests. The admission controller retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a third-party email provider.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the inventory service did not restore service and left the MySQL replica set in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the MySQL replica set in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the inventory service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The ingest gateway timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in ap-southeast were routed to the object store bucket in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the object store bucket and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the documents table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the DynamoDB table, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the DynamoDB table, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.

issue: The document indexer was degraded for 3 hours 20 minutes because of a fault at an upstream payment processor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The session store had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Added response validation in the session store so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Users reported the notification service being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the reporting UI issued one request per item rather than a single batched call. Each individual request was fast, so backend metrics stayed normal while the aggregate page load grew to several seconds. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 23 minutes, while the payments themselves completed normally.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the rate limiter made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Alerting was keyed on error rate rather than on completion rate, so a silent stall produced no signal.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the rate limiter to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: The entitlement service affected by an infrastructure event.

The entitlement service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Served a degraded response while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Writes to the audit table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the media transcoder for 3 hours 20 minutes.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the audit table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the search API made the incident worse and extended impact by 14 minutes.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Elasticsearch index, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Elasticsearch index, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Processing in the messaging bridge did not complete as expected.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced a regional fault. The messaging bridge depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.

issue: Background jobs in the media transcoder stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of two thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the events table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the admission controller rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the admission controller to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: 55% of API responses from the pricing engine could return records belonging to another tenant. Impact was limited to two of three availability zones.
root_cause: A caching layer added in front of the pricing engine keyed entries without the tenant identifier, so a response generated for one tenant could be served to another.
solution: Added the tenant identifier to the cache key, invalidated the cache entirely, and added a test asserting that a response generated for one tenant is never served to another. Credentials were reissued with least-privilege scope and the remaining set was audited for excessive permissions.

issue: Elevated query latency against the SQLite metadata store. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A query plan on the events table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The sync service degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 63% of queries exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: A query plan on the entitlements table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in us-east.
root_cause: The reporting UI began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: Background jobs in the billing service stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of three thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the health checker selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty.

issue: The ingest gateway unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A feature flag for the ingest gateway was created with a default-on value rather than default-off. The flag service treats an absent per-tenant override as the default, so every tenant without an explicit override received the new behaviour.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time.

issue: The geocoding service was degraded for 1 hour 12 minutes because of an outage at a partner inventory feed. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning errors for a subset of requests. The batch consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a partner inventory feed.

issue: A migration on the sessions table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the Elasticsearch index. The affected replicas entered recovery, which pushed their load onto the remainder and cascaded into a broader capacity shortfall.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the admin console.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The batch consumer had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Added response validation in the batch consumer so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The partner API unreachable for a subset of clients. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the entitlement service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: The webhook dispatcher could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in sa-east.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the webhook dispatcher was raised past what any node in sa-east could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Lower-priority processing in eu-central was delayed by 1 hour 12 minutes during planned maintenance.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in eu-central, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: The catalogue API became slow in eu-central only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in eu-central left the catalogue API running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in eu-central and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the catalogue API, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the catalogue API failed to reconnect after a restart of the config loader and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: The feed builder failed to start in the primary region after a dependency upgrade, and 85% of requests to the webhooks endpoint returned errors.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the shard mapper to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: The billing service silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the documents table without updates.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the MongoDB shard was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Database errors affecting the inventory service.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the Cassandra ring stalled without raising an error.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness.

issue: The scheduling service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the scheduling service, and the rule applied to production rather than a single tenant. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the notification service.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the notification service failed to reconnect after a restart of the job scheduler and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
