solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: The inventory service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-northeast.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the inventory service did not set, so the rate limiter silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the rate limiter to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Requests to the embedded widget failed TLS negotiation for 24% of clients starting at a fixed time of day.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded. Retries did not help because the resolution step failed before any connection was attempted.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy.

issue: The search API stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 2 hours 5 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the entitlements table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the config loader rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The query planner had no recent statistics for the affected relation, so it continued choosing a plan that no longer suited the data.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the config loader to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Processing in the checkout service did not complete as expected. Impact was limited to the primary region.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The checkout service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The admin console began returning errors for 31% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the reporting API itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the reporting API started with settings it could not validate. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the reporting API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Scheduled disbursements in the document indexer did not execute on their intended date.
root_cause: A timezone change in the scheduling configuration for the document indexer moved the payout cutoff past the window during which a third-party email provider accepts same-day instructions, so batches were held until the next cycle.
solution: Restored the scheduling configuration to the correct timezone and pinned the cutoff to the processor's stated window rather than a local time.

issue: The audit log writer degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the audit log writer, and the rule applied to production rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the document indexer in us-east.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning errors for a subset of requests. The admission controller retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. The redundancy that was expected to cover this failure shared an upstream component with the path that failed.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the upstream CDN.

issue: All inbound traffic to the media transcoder stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the media transcoder was drawn away from its intended path. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the checkout service in eu-central.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: Errors on the partner API following a recent change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the webhook dispatcher did not set, so the token validator silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the token validator to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: A scheduled job in the checkout service did not run for 3 hours 20 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the checkout service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur.

issue: Reports generated by the reporting API contained figures that did not reconcile with the underlying records.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the reporting API placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. A cached fallback and status indicator were added so an upstream fault degrades the feature rather than removing it.

issue: A scheduled job in the media transcoder did not run for 6 hours 10 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the media transcoder was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the ingest gateway started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the ingest gateway within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Read and write errors against the DynamoDB table.
root_cause: A query plan on the orders table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: An unauthorised party obtained access to secrets used by the chat backend, affecting a small subset of integrations.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed was itself compromised, and the data it held on behalf of the organisation included access tokens and keys issued for customer integrations with the chat backend.
solution: Suspended affected integrations immediately, then coordinated with each provider to revoke and reissue every token and key that had been held, rotating internal credentials before resuming service.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the messaging bridge made the incident worse and extended impact by 38 minutes.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Redis cache tier, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Redis cache tier, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The billing service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the billing service was raised past what any node in us-east could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Access to the embedded widget denied for a subset of users.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the serialisation layer caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the serialisation layer, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: The admin console unreachable for a subset of clients.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the export worker were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path.

issue: The partner API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: The partner API began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time.

issue: Potential data exposure involving the inventory service. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A prototype machine had never been decommissioned and was still running software with a known unpatched vulnerability.
solution: Took the affected systems offline, rotated every credential the host had held, and introduced a decommissioning process that revokes credentials and network access as part of retirement.

issue: A traffic spike on the mobile apps pushed the catalogue API past its capacity and 11% of requests failed.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the catalogue API for every caller.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth.

issue: Federated login to the messaging bridge broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the shard mapper caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. Because tokens are cached by clients, the impact appeared gradually as existing tokens expired.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the shard mapper, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the webhook dispatcher unable to serve traffic in a single production cell.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The health checker had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the health checker to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: 55% of requests to the admin console failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The ingest gateway depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because every internal component reported healthy, responders spent much of the incident ruling out their own systems.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Sign-in and authorisation errors on the mobile apps.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the metrics agent uses to validate credentials for the identity service.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. Validation changes are staged behind a per-tenant warning period before they are enforced.

issue: A traffic spike on the CLI pushed the scheduling service past its capacity and 94% of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the scheduling service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the scheduling service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Scheduled disbursements in the recommendation service did not execute on their intended date.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the batch consumer rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field. Those payouts were queued rather than failed, so they accumulated silently until the delay was noticed.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the batch consumer to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the webhooks endpoint.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The job scheduler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Added response validation in the job scheduler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the production fleet. Both the webhooks endpoint and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the inventory service responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the request router expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The pricing engine shedding requests under load.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the connection pool identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. The affected path had no concurrency limit, so a single slow dependency was enough to occupy every available worker.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the connection pool so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: The embedded widget began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the ingest gateway itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the ingest gateway started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the ingest gateway within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Internal name resolution failed across production and services could no longer reach one another for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting production. The defect was not caught in pre-production because the test environment resolved names through a different path, so it first appeared in production. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: The identity service was degraded for 4 hours 36 minutes because of a fault at an upstream payment processor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor experienced a regional fault. The identity service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an upstream payment processor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Calls to the feed builder were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 55% of clients. Impact was limited to us-east.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the token validator identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the token validator so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: 24% of reads served by the sync service reflected data minutes behind the primary.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the primary Postgres cluster, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The feed builder unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the feed builder. The new default disagreed with the sidecar proxy, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the sidecar proxy cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: The SQLite metadata store became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the SQLite metadata store.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: 11% of requests to the CLI were served by an unintended backend for 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the billing service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the asset pipeline, and the rule applied to the primary cluster rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop.

issue: The messaging bridge processing work incorrectly under concurrency.
root_cause: The batch consumer read a value, computed a new one and wrote it back without a transaction or compare-and-set. Concurrent requests for the same record interleaved between the read and the write, so one update silently overwrote the other. Recovery required restarting the affected processes, since nothing detected a worker that had stopped making progress.
solution: Repaired the affected records and changed the update to a single conditional write so a concurrent modification fails and retries rather than being lost.

issue: Potential data exposure involving the catalogue API. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: An attack targeted an endpoint on the catalogue API whose responses were expensive to generate and not cached, so a modest request rate was enough to exhaust backend capacity.
solution: Added caching and a strict rate limit to the expensive endpoint, and placed it behind authentication so it cannot be reached anonymously at volume.

issue: A subset of transactions in the catalogue API were recorded twice over a 14 minutes window. Impact was limited to sa-east.
root_cause: A retry in the rate limiter re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to the cloud provider block-storage service so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: New deployments of the catalogue API hung in a pending state for 1 hour 12 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the catalogue API did not set, so the session store silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the session store to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Single sign-on to the mobile apps failed for 78% of enterprise tenants for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the session store caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. Service-to-service calls used the same validation path, so internal workflows failed alongside end-user sign-in.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the session store, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the reporting API.
root_cause: A cache key for the reporting API included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the MySQL replica set. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Payment failures affecting the webhooks endpoint.
root_cause: A change to the queue infrastructure behind the scheduling service caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection without raising an error.
solution: Replayed the undelivered callbacks once identified, then added active health checks on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: Requests to the mobile apps failed TLS negotiation for the majority of clients starting at a fixed time of day.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the feed builder expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Traffic to the billing service failing to reach its destination.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect a single production cell to the outside world. The same change removed the paths engineers would have used to reach the equipment remotely.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: Elevated query latency against the MySQL replica set.
root_cause: An index on the webhooks table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the MySQL replica set.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The pricing engine could not create new records, returning a database-level error unrelated to any application change.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the accounts table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The feed builder was removed from rotation in the primary region despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 55%. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the feed builder responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the metrics agent expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Requests to the sync service failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the sync service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the sync service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Sign-in to the partner API failed intermittently while other functionality remained available.
root_cause: A signing key used by the connection pool was rotated without updating every validator, so tokens issued after the rotation were rejected by the services still holding the previous key. Affected users retried repeatedly, which added load to the same component that was already failing.
solution: Distributed the new key to all validators and changed rotation to publish the new key and accept both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Reduced availability in sa-east. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the scheduling service were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Name lookups for the mobile apps returned errors for 2 hours 5 minutes, with a period of total failure during recovery.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the recommendation service still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Every service that resolved the affected name failed together, which made the blast radius far larger than the change implied.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the ingest gateway made the incident worse and extended impact by 2 hours 5 minutes.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the Cassandra ring in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the ingest gateway failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the billing service did not restore service and left the object store bucket in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the object store bucket in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the billing service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Writes to the subscriptions table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the entitlement service for 6 hours 10 minutes. Both the reporting UI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the subscriptions table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Authentication requests to the media transcoder timed out for a small subset of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: Session records in the MongoDB shard were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the session store. Affected users retried repeatedly, which added load to the same component that was already failing.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once.

issue: The chat backend ran with configuration from the previous release for 3 hours 20 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the chat backend stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the chat backend actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The media transcoder was degraded for 4 hours 36 minutes because of an outage at a third-party email provider.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning errors for a subset of requests. The metrics agent retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a third-party email provider.

issue: The SDK slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the geocoding service. As requests queued, client retries added further load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: The webhooks endpoint displayed incorrect values to 3% of users for 51 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A rounding change in the config loader was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports.

issue: 11% of test runs against the export worker failed unpredictably after a performance change.
root_cause: Shared state in the token validator was accessed without synchronisation from a callback that could run on a different thread, so corruption appeared only when the callback overlapped with a request. The defect had been present for some time and surfaced only once traffic shape changed enough to hit the interleaving.
solution: Confined the shared state behind a single owner and added a race detector to the test pipeline so this class of defect fails the build.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the document indexer.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the document indexer failed to reconnect after a restart of the batch consumer and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: 24% of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the inventory service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: 78% of requests to the partner API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The connection pool had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the connection pool so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The pricing engine was degraded for 4 hours 36 minutes because of an outage at the managed Kubernetes control plane.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced an outage in two of three availability zones.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The webhooks endpoint began returning errors for 31% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the search API itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the search API started with settings it could not validate. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the search API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Healthy instances of the catalogue API were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 9 hours window.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the catalogue API responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the config loader expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the checkout service unable to serve traffic in production.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the config loader still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in production. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The pricing engine failed to start in sa-east after a dependency upgrade, and 63% of requests to the SDK returned errors.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The retry handler had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the retry handler to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The checkout service unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the checkout service was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges.

issue: 94% of requests to the partner API were served by an unintended backend for 1 hour 47 minutes.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the recommendation service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: 85% of programmatic clients lost access to the admin console without any credential change on their side.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the batch consumer was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover.

issue: The recommendation service shedding requests under load.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the Frankfurt region left the recommendation service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in the Frankfurt region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the inventory service.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting the shared staging-to-production path. The defect was not caught in pre-production because the test environment resolved names through a different path, so it first appeared in production.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production.

issue: Queries against the subscriptions table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the identity service began timing out for 63% of requests. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A new query against the subscriptions table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the MongoDB shard.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: The identity service degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the rate limiter selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The MySQL replica set became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the MySQL replica set. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Single sign-on to the webhooks endpoint failed for 94% of enterprise tenants for 9 hours.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the job scheduler. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Because tokens are cached by clients, the impact appeared gradually as existing tokens expired.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period.

issue: Federated login to the billing service broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the admission controller. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the scheduling service across the primary cluster.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the ClickHouse cluster, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the ClickHouse cluster, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The checkout service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the devices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the serialisation layer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the serialisation layer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: All inbound traffic to the ingest gateway stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect the production fleet to the outside world. The same change removed the paths engineers would have used to reach the equipment remotely. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: Federated login to the entitlement service broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the batch consumer. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Because the failure was in the credential path rather than the application, every feature behind sign-in became unreachable.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period. A pre-apply check now lists every resource a policy change will affect before it is applied.

issue: The catalogue API was degraded for 2 hours 5 minutes because of a fault at an external geolocation API rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced a regional fault. The catalogue API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

issue: Latency on the notification service was 55% higher in one region for 6 hours 10 minutes with no configuration difference. Impact was limited to eu-west.
root_cause: Instances of the notification service in eu-west were routed to the SQLite metadata store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. The affected path had no concurrency limit, so a single slow dependency was enough to occupy every available worker.
solution: Repointed the notification service at the local replica of the SQLite metadata store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Database errors affecting the feed builder.
root_cause: A query plan on the accounts table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: A traffic spike on the mobile apps pushed the entitlement service past its capacity and 31% of requests failed. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the entitlement service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete. Queues grew past the queue depth limit and requests began failing after already consuming capacity. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Added admission control so the entitlement service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: The billing service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the billing service. The new default disagreed with the session store, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the session store cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the geocoding service did not restore service and left the MySQL replica set in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the MySQL replica set, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the MySQL replica set, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the entitlement service stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the entitlement service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: A low-risk change to all regions resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The change was tested against a single node but applied to the fleet simultaneously, so a defect that one node could absorb removed capacity everywhere at once. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Reverted the change and introduced staged application across the fleet with a health gate between stages.

issue: The entitlement service silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the orders table without updates. Impact was limited to the Sydney region.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the entitlement service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. A cached fallback and status indicator were added so an upstream fault degrades the feature rather than removing it.

issue: The export worker unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the shared staging-to-production path because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the export worker started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the export worker within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A migration on the orders table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the orders table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Infrastructure fault degrading the webhook dispatcher.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the webhook dispatcher were found to share an upstream component. When that component failed, both feeds dropped together despite the design being described as redundant.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths.

issue: Batch workloads on the document indexer ran at reduced throughput for 23 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in ap-southeast, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region.

issue: The identity service shedding requests under load.
root_cause: Instances of the identity service in ap-southeast were routed to the Elasticsearch index in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the identity service at the local replica of the Elasticsearch index and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Queries against the documents table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the notification service began timing out for 11% of requests. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A new query against the documents table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the DynamoDB table. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The catalogue API degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and cache hit rate on the Elasticsearch index rose steadily for 2 hours 5 minutes.
root_cause: A schema migration on the webhooks table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create.

issue: Routing for the pricing engine sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting 42% of traffic.
root_cause: An edge configuration set the backend target inside a request handler, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the target to the first entry in the list rather than the intended one. Negative results were cached downstream, so the failure persisted for some clients after the underlying record was corrected.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test that asserts backend selection after a mid-request restart.

issue: Network errors between services in production. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the identity service still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: 31% of requests to the identity service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure. Impact was limited to ap-northeast.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The identity service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The asset pipeline silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the entitlements table without updates.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the Elasticsearch index was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: Access to the admin console denied for a subset of users.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the leader elector uses to validate credentials for the recommendation service. Service-to-service calls used the same validation path, so internal workflows failed alongside end-user sign-in.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: Read and write errors against the MySQL replica set.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the MySQL replica set stalled without raising an error. Monitoring tracked replica availability but not replication lag, so the stall was invisible until customers reported inconsistency.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness.

issue: Capacity in the primary region fell by 63% and the recommendation service began shedding requests.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the recommendation service, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Latency on the chat backend was 18% higher in one region for 2 hours 5 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the chat backend in the Sydney region were routed to the Redis cache tier in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Repointed the chat backend at the local replica of the Redis cache tier and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: Healthy instances of the checkout service were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 1 hour 47 minutes window.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Writes to the orders table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the reporting API for most of the working day.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the orders table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: 94% of requests to the pricing engine were rejected at the edge while the service itself reported healthy.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the pricing engine, and the rule applied to the primary cluster rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The sync service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the mobile apps.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The session store had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Because every internal component reported healthy, responders spent much of the incident ruling out their own systems.
solution: Added response validation in the session store so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The feed builder ran with configuration from the previous release for 2 hours 5 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the feed builder stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the feed builder actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: The export worker was degraded for 1 hour 12 minutes because of a fault at a partner inventory feed rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The job scheduler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Added response validation in the job scheduler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the ingest gateway did not restore service and left the primary Postgres cluster in a state neither version could read. Both the admin console and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the primary Postgres cluster, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the primary Postgres cluster, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The catalogue API stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 9 hours.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the session store selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The asset pipeline ran with configuration from the previous release for 1 hour 47 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the cache layer but the asset pipeline reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Requests to the ingest gateway failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the shared staging-to-production path because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the ingest gateway started with settings it could not validate. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the ingest gateway within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was unavailable for 38 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the DynamoDB table. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the billing service. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced a regional fault. The billing service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was degraded for 1 hour 47 minutes because of a fault at a third-party email provider rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The shard mapper had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the shard mapper so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Requests to the messaging bridge failed across a single production cell immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the messaging bridge started with settings it could not validate. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the messaging bridge within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The ClickHouse cluster became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the ClickHouse cluster.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the ingest gateway.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the Elasticsearch index did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the leader elector could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the Elasticsearch index and changed the leader elector to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. A pre-apply check now lists every resource a policy change will affect before it is applied.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to production.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the webhook dispatcher stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
