solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the webhook dispatcher actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: The geocoding service was degraded for 6 hours 10 minutes because of an outage at the managed DNS provider.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning errors for a subset of requests. The token validator retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the managed DNS provider.

issue: The billing service degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and cache hit rate on the MongoDB shard rose steadily for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A new query against the accounts table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the MongoDB shard. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: The chat backend was degraded for 2 hours 5 minutes because of an outage at the managed Kubernetes control plane.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced an outage in ap-southeast. The chat backend called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The geocoding service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the rate limiter selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: 42% of requests to the admin console failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The request router had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Added response validation in the request router so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: 42% of payment attempts on the web dashboard timed out for 51 minutes during a demand surge.
root_cause: The sync service could not scale out to meet the surge because its resource configuration prevented new instances from being placed, even though spare capacity existed.
solution: Corrected the resource configuration so instances could be scheduled onto available capacity, and added load testing ahead of promotional events to surface scaling limits in advance. Completion rate is now alerted alongside error rate so a silent stall produces a signal.

issue: The feed builder degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The job scheduler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Added response validation in the job scheduler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Intermittent connection failures in us-west.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting the production fleet. The defect was not caught in pre-production because the test environment resolved names through a different path, so it first appeared in production.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: The sync service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 4 hours 36 minutes. Impact was limited to the Sydney region.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the entitlements table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the shard mapper rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the shard mapper to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the media transcoder stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the media transcoder actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the reporting API in us-east. Both the public API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced an outage in us-east. The reporting API called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Served a degraded response while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: Data access failures in the production fleet.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the orders table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the config loader rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the config loader to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Requests to the notification service failed across the primary cluster immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the notification service. The new default disagreed with the token validator, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the token validator cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the SDK was blocked for most of the working day with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the messaging bridge, and the rule applied to all regions rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop.

issue: The billing service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the billing service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the billing service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The geocoding service ran with configuration from the previous release for 14 minutes even though the deploy reported success. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the session store but the geocoding service reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Latency on the notification service was 31% higher in one region for 6 hours 10 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in us-east left the notification service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in us-east and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: The ingest gateway was unavailable for 1 hour 47 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the time-series store. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Elevated response times on the public API.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in two of three availability zones were routed to the MySQL replica set in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the MySQL replica set and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The feed builder was degraded for most of the working day because of a fault at a partner inventory feed rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The retry handler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Added response validation in the retry handler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. A cached fallback and status indicator were added so an upstream fault degrades the feature rather than removing it.

issue: The checkout service was degraded for 1 hour 47 minutes because of an outage at a downstream KYC vendor. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning errors for a subset of requests. The job scheduler retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Recovery required physical intervention, so time to repair was governed by access rather than by diagnosis.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a downstream KYC vendor.

issue: Elevated query latency against the MySQL replica set.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the webhooks table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: Background jobs in the feed builder stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of dozens of thousand items accumulated. Impact was limited to two of three availability zones.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the events table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the cache layer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the cache layer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The sync service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A feature flag for the sync service was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The document indexer availability fell by 7% during the last stage of a long-running schema change. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the orders table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The reporting UI began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the search API itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the search API. The new default disagreed with the request router, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the request router cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Calls to the entitlement service were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 31% of clients.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the config loader treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the pricing engine unable to serve traffic in production.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The token validator had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the token validator to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the SDK.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The metrics agent had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Added response validation in the metrics agent so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: 85% of API clients received throttling responses from the scheduling service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the token validator identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the token validator so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Just under half of requests to the CLI failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The sidecar proxy had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Added response validation in the sidecar proxy so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The public API began returning errors for 85% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the chat backend itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the chat backend started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the chat backend within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A migration on the entitlements table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the entitlements table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Request throughput on the billing service rose from normal to several seconds, and 85% of calls to the SDK exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: The metrics agent began synchronously calling a partner inventory feed on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to a partner inventory feed back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: A feature intended for internal testing became active for a small subset of customers on the reporting UI without an announcement.
root_cause: A feature flag for the identity service was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Request throughput on the ingest gateway rose from normal to several seconds, and 63% of calls to the reporting UI exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the ingest gateway. As requests queued, client retries added further load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Replication lag on the pricing engine rose from normal to several seconds, and 18% of calls to the CLI exceeded their timeout. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The connection pool began synchronously calling the managed DNS provider on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to the managed DNS provider back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: All inbound traffic to the search API stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the search API was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: A traffic spike on the admin console pushed the asset pipeline past its capacity and 42% of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the asset pipeline had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the asset pipeline rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: 7% of requests to the reporting UI failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The upstream CDN experienced a regional fault. The chat backend depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the upstream CDN recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Users were unable to sign in or load the mobile apps platform-wide, with error rates climbing for 9 hours.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the Kafka topic past what it could serve. The automated protective throttle was initially tuned too aggressively and had to be corrected in smaller steps.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions. Error responses now distinguish an infrastructure failure from an invalid credential so support can triage correctly.

issue: The inventory service availability fell by 55% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the Kafka topic.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock.

issue: The reporting API degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the ClickHouse cluster, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the ClickHouse cluster, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The geocoding service ran with configuration from the previous release for 4 hours 36 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the health checker but the geocoding service reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the media transcoder did not restore service and left the Kafka topic in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Kafka topic, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Kafka topic, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The feed builder was degraded for 51 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The admission controller had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the admission controller so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The inventory service unavailable due to a database fault.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the time-series store.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the identity service.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the SQLite metadata store past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the web dashboard was blocked for 51 minutes with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the feed builder, and the rule applied to production rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Routing for the geocoding service sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting a handful of traffic.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the geocoding service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: An unauthorised party obtained access to secrets used by the inventory service, affecting a handful of integrations. Both the webhooks endpoint and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service was itself compromised, and the data it held on behalf of the organisation included access tokens and keys issued for customer integrations with the inventory service.
solution: Suspended affected integrations immediately, then coordinated with each provider to revoke and reissue every token and key that had been held, rotating internal credentials before resuming service.

issue: The entitlement service returned elevated errors for 4 hours 36 minutes after a sudden increase in inbound volume.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the entitlement service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the entitlement service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Reads from the pricing engine returned stale data for 3 hours 20 minutes while writes continued to succeed normally.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the DynamoDB table, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically.

issue: The pricing engine affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the pricing engine, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Data access failures in the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the SQLite metadata store. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied.

A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Data access failures in the primary cluster.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the object store bucket, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the session store to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the SDK.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the primary cluster was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Errors on the SDK following a recent change.
root_cause: A feature flag for the asset pipeline was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in us-west.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the export worker had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the export worker rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Callers of the search API saw response times multiply for 2 hours 5 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The admission controller began synchronously calling an external geolocation API on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to an external geolocation API back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Credential validation failures in the primary cluster.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the config loader. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Garbage-collection pause time on the ClickHouse cluster rose steadily over 2 hours 5 minutes and the pricing engine began shedding requests, with no change in traffic volume.
root_cause: An index on the documents table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the ClickHouse cluster.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: The asset pipeline affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced an outage in us-east. The asset pipeline called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Dozens of hundred payments were double-counted in the ledger table before the discrepancy was detected.
root_cause: A failover of the MySQL replica set mid-transaction left a partial record. The reconciliation job treated the partial row as missing and re-submitted it, producing a duplicate.
solution: Reversed the duplicates, and changed reconciliation to resolve a partial record against the processor's ledger before re-submitting anything.

issue: Payment failures affecting the SDK. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A timezone change in the scheduling configuration for the messaging bridge moved the payout cutoff past the window during which a downstream KYC vendor accepts same-day instructions, so batches were held until the next cycle.
solution: Restored the scheduling configuration to the correct timezone and pinned the cutoff to the processor's stated window rather than a local time.

issue: The recommendation service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in the Frankfurt region, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region.

issue: Infrastructure fault degrading the notification service.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the notification service were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: An unused host was found to be an entry point through which an attacker reached the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A host removed from active service retained its network access and service account. Nothing reconciled the inventory against issued credentials, so the stale access went unnoticed. Audit logging covered the application but not the administrative path that was used, which complicated scoping.
solution: Revoked the stale access and added periodic reconciliation between the host inventory and issued credentials so orphaned access is detected automatically. Risk-proportional review requirements were adopted so a change of that scope cannot be labelled routine.

issue: The inventory service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the inventory service did not set, so the request router silently rejected every new instance. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the request router to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: The SDK began returning errors for just under half of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the audit log writer itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the audit log writer started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the audit log writer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The asset pipeline timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the metrics agent treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: The admin console unreachable for a subset of clients.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect the shared staging-to-production path to the outside world.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: The webhook dispatcher degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and cache hit rate on the Kafka topic rose steadily for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A schema migration on the invoices table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification. For the window where the index did not exist, queries that depended on it fell back to full scans and saturated the Kafka topic.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the primary cluster.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the audit log writer did not set, so the serialisation layer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the serialisation layer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Several hundred hundred payments were double-counted in the sessions table before the discrepancy was detected.
root_cause: A retry in the config loader re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to the cloud provider block-storage service so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: The reporting UI began returning errors for 18% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the billing service itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the billing service. The new default disagreed with the sidecar proxy, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the sidecar proxy cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: Roughly a third of requests to the public API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor experienced a regional fault. The document indexer depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an upstream payment processor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Errors on the webhooks endpoint following a recent change. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The config loader had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the config loader to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: The inventory service degraded after a routine rollout. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the inventory service, and the rule applied to a single production cell rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Single sign-on to the partner API failed for the majority of enterprise tenants for 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the config loader. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Monitoring covered availability of the endpoint rather than successful authentication, so it stayed green.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the audit log writer.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced a regional fault. The audit log writer depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The webhooks endpoint slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the reporting API had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the reporting API rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: The Cassandra ring became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the Cassandra ring. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: A migration on the subscriptions table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the object store bucket.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock.

issue: Requests to the checkout service queued and timed out while the object store bucket itself remained lightly loaded. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The connection pool for the checkout service was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the object store bucket would accept and new connections were refused. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Elevated query latency against the time-series store.
root_cause: A schema migration on the devices table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create.

issue: A maintenance window on the primary cluster that was expected to be routine caused 51 minutes of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the primary cluster was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Intermittent connection failures in the primary region.
root_cause: A static routing configuration had not kept pace with infrastructure growth, so updated discovery information could not reach every consumer. Clients continued working from a stale view and sent traffic to instances that had been replaced.
solution: Restored discovery data to the affected consumers and changed the routing configuration to scale with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: A subset of transactions in the reporting API were recorded twice over a 3 hours 20 minutes window.
root_cause: A retry in the queue consumer re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to an external geolocation API so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: A small subset of API clients received throttling responses from the sync service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the retry handler identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the retry handler so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Read and write errors against the Elasticsearch index. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the admission controller selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: The CLI displayed incorrect values to 11% of users for 4 hours 36 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A rounding change in the serialisation layer was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Elevated response times on the embedded widget.
root_cause: Instances of the reporting API in the Sydney region were routed to the ClickHouse cluster in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the reporting API at the local replica of the ClickHouse cluster and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly. Load shedding was added so the service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline.

issue: 24% of reads served by the billing service reflected data minutes behind the primary. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Redis cache tier, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Elevated query latency against the time-series store.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the ledger table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: All regions lost external connectivity for 1 hour 47 minutes, including the remote access paths needed to diagnose the problem.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect all regions to the outside world.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane.

issue: The feed builder degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the sidecar proxy but the feed builder reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The media transcoder was offline for 6 hours 10 minutes after a power event at the facility hosting production. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting production was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed. Key details of the provider's failover arrangement had not been documented in advance, which slowed diagnosis. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events.

issue: The checkout service became unreachable for external clients while internal callers were unaffected.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the checkout service expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Internal callers were affected while external monitoring continued to pass, so detection relied on customer reports.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the document indexer stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the document indexer actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: Processing in the feed builder did not complete as expected.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The retry handler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the retry handler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Writes to the sessions table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the entitlement service for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the sessions table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The scheduling service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the primary Postgres cluster, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the primary Postgres cluster, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the web dashboard was blocked for 51 minutes with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A filtering rule was changed directly on the edge tier outside the normal pipeline, so the change did not appear in deployment history. Responders spent most of the incident examining recent releases before drift detection surfaced the untracked edit. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band edge change and restricted write access so edits outside the pipeline are blocked, with drift detection alerting on any that still occur. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Data access failures in all regions. Impact was limited to ap-northeast.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the webhooks table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the job scheduler rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the job scheduler to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The recommendation service degraded by a datastore problem. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the audit table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the request router rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the request router to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: The asset pipeline became slow in ap-southeast only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: Instances of the asset pipeline in ap-southeast were routed to the Kafka topic in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the asset pipeline at the local replica of the Kafka topic and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Intermittent failures in the webhook dispatcher under load.
root_cause: A uniqueness check in the webhook dispatcher was performed as a read followed by an insert. Two concurrent requests both passed the read before either inserted, producing duplicate records that later code assumed could not exist.
solution: De-duplicated the records and enforced uniqueness with a database constraint rather than an application-level check, so the guarantee holds under concurrency. A race detector was added to the test pipeline so this class of defect fails the build.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the SQLite metadata store, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the SQLite metadata store, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Errors on the mobile apps following a recent change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the messaging bridge started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the messaging bridge within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Connection count on the scheduling service rose from normal to several seconds, and 24% of calls to the embedded widget exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: The metrics agent began synchronously calling a third-party email provider on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to a third-party email provider back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: A maintenance window on the primary cluster that was expected to be routine caused 51 minutes of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the primary cluster was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly.

issue: Background jobs in the ingest gateway stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of a handful of thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the accounts table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the cache layer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the cache layer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: All regions lost external connectivity for 4 hours 36 minutes, including the remote access paths needed to diagnose the problem.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the sync service was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: The audit log writer unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: A script restarted only the authoritative resolver after an address change and left the caching resolver untouched, so cached lookups began timing out.
solution: Rebuilt and republished a correct zone by hand, restarted both resolvers, and added a rule that DNS-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a DNS outage.

issue: Connection count on the geocoding service rose from normal to several seconds, and 85% of calls to the webhooks endpoint exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: The connection pool began synchronously calling a partner inventory feed on a path that had previously been asynchronous. Each request inherited the dependency latency, and the thread pool filled with waiting work.
solution: Moved the call to a partner inventory feed back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: 7% of requests to the sync service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in two of three availability zones. The sync service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was removed from rotation in two of three availability zones despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 3%. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the webhook dispatcher responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the request router expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Credential validation failures in all regions.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the session store caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the session store, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: Latency on the pricing engine was 24% higher in one region for most of the working day with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the primary region left the pricing engine running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in the primary region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: The media transcoder affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A node in ap-southeast entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: Capacity in eu-west fell by 3% and the entitlement service began shedding requests.
root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in eu-west below what was needed to serve normal traffic. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the shortfall.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: The document indexer exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected 18% of requests.
root_cause: The connection pool for the document indexer was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the Redis cache tier would accept and new connections were refused. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the entitlement service, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the entitlement service failed to reconnect after a restart of the cache layer and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: The messaging bridge unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Elasticsearch index, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Elasticsearch index, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Work assigned to one node in eu-central stalled for 2 hours 5 minutes while the node remained in rotation. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A node in eu-central entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations. The probe tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: Memory growth in the export worker leading to restarts.
root_cause: An unbounded in-process cache in the job scheduler had no eviction policy. It grew in proportion to the number of distinct keys seen, which rose continuously with traffic. Because only one environment was affected, the problem was initially attributed to that environment rather than the code.
solution: Added a size limit and least-recently-used eviction to the cache, and added an alert on memory growth over a rolling window rather than only on process restarts.

issue: Requests to the reporting API failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the reporting API. The new default disagreed with the token validator, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the token validator cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Credential validation failures in a single production cell.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the primary Postgres cluster did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the retry handler could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the primary Postgres cluster and changed the retry handler to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the ingest gateway.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded. The change looked routine in review because its effect depended on which resolver path a caller happened to use.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: Users reported the chat backend being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the public API issued one request per item rather than a single batched call.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: Single sign-on to the partner API failed for 7% of enterprise tenants for most of the working day.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the request router. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Because tokens are cached by clients, the impact appeared gradually as existing tokens expired.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: A low-risk change to a single production cell resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving a single production cell was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

issue: The export worker was offline for 38 minutes after a power event at the facility hosting the primary cluster.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the export worker were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: The reporting API degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and the majority of queries exceeded their timeout.
