root_cause: An index on the audit table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the Cassandra ring. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the entitlement service in all regions.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the entitlement service stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the entitlement service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: Unauthorised activity detected in the primary cluster. Impact was limited to the primary region.
root_cause: A credential with broader permissions than it needed was stored in the object store bucket in recoverable form.
solution: Revoked the exposed credential, reissued it with least-privilege scope, moved secret storage to a managed service with audited access, and audited remaining credentials for excessive permissions.

issue: The embedded widget displayed incorrect values to 24% of users for 1 hour 47 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the scheduling service placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records.

issue: Eight hundred payments were double-counted in the subscriptions table before the discrepancy was detected.
root_cause: A retry in the connection pool re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost. Without an idempotency key, the cloud provider block-storage service treated the retry as a new transaction.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to the cloud provider block-storage service so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: A power interruption took production offline and recovery took considerably longer than planned.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the inventory service were found to share an upstream component. When that component failed, both feeds dropped together despite the design being described as redundant.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: A maintenance window on a single production cell that was expected to be routine caused 23 minutes of unplanned downtime. Both the public API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving a single production cell was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly.

issue: 85% of requests to the mobile apps failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The checkout service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A maintenance window on all regions that was expected to be routine caused 14 minutes of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving all regions was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The chat backend degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The job scheduler had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the job scheduler to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Requests to the mobile apps failed TLS negotiation for the majority of clients starting at a fixed time of day.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the reporting API expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently.

issue: The billing service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the session store selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty.

issue: Callers of the billing service saw response times multiply for 2 hours 5 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The serialisation layer began synchronously calling the upstream CDN on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to the upstream CDN back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: The feed builder returned elevated errors for 3 hours 20 minutes after a sudden increase in inbound volume.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the feed builder for every caller. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth.

issue: 85% of requests to the SDK failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane began returning malformed responses rather than errors.
solution: Added response validation in the shard mapper so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Data access failures in the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the DynamoDB table, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically.

issue: The geocoding service unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the geocoding service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: The recommendation service was unavailable for most of the working day and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the primary Postgres cluster. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The partner API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: The job scheduler began synchronously calling an external geolocation API on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to an external geolocation API back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: The entitlement service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in two of three availability zones.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the entitlement service was raised past what any node in two of three availability zones could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the asset pipeline started with settings it could not validate. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the asset pipeline within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Background jobs in the reporting API stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of dozens of thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the session store selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Users reported the media transcoder being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the partner API issued one request per item rather than a single batched call. Each individual request was fast, so backend metrics stayed normal while the aggregate page load grew to several seconds.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Payouts from the geocoding service were delayed by 23 minutes for 3% of recipients.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the metrics agent rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the metrics agent to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the recommendation service made the incident worse and extended impact by 38 minutes.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the MongoDB shard in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the recommendation service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer.

issue: The catalogue API ran with configuration from the previous release for 9 hours even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the catalogue API stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the catalogue API actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the messaging bridge stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the messaging bridge actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The feed builder failed to start in sa-east after a dependency upgrade, and 24% of requests to the reporting UI returned errors.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The token validator had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the token validator to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Writes to the accounts table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the webhook dispatcher for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the accounts table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted.

issue: The webhook dispatcher consumed increasing memory in one environment only, while the same build was stable elsewhere.
root_cause: Memory was lost to fragmentation rather than a genuine leak. An aligned-allocation pattern in the connection pool interacted poorly with the system allocator in that environment, permanently fragmenting the pool even though every allocation was correctly freed. Instances were restarted automatically on termination, which masked the underlying growth from everyone but the on-call engineer.
solution: Replaced the aligned-allocation pattern with a dedicated allocator that avoids the fragmenting path, which stopped the steady growth under sustained load. A bound was placed on the retained structure so its size no longer tracks process lifetime.

issue: Callers of the inventory service saw response times multiply for 6 hours 10 minutes under ordinary traffic. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: The leader elector began synchronously calling the managed Kubernetes control plane on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to the managed Kubernetes control plane back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Latency on the feed builder was 31% higher in one region for 1 hour 47 minutes with no configuration difference. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the Frankfurt region left the feed builder running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Restored the instance count in the Frankfurt region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: The catalogue API was degraded for most of the working day because of an outage at a partner inventory feed.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning errors for a subset of requests. The request router retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a partner inventory feed.

issue: The pricing engine degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the MySQL replica set. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure.

issue: The inventory service was removed from rotation in the primary region despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 55%.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The catalogue API exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected 63% of requests.
root_cause: The connection pool for the catalogue API was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the Cassandra ring would accept and new connections were refused. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value.

issue: Access to the SDK denied for a subset of users.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the primary Postgres cluster did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the metrics agent could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the primary Postgres cluster and changed the metrics agent to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The audit log writer unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the audit log writer started with settings it could not validate. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the audit log writer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Elevated response times on the mobile apps.
root_cause: The mobile apps began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time. Load shedding was added so the service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline.

issue: Potential data exposure involving the messaging bridge.
root_cause: A credential with broader permissions than it needed was stored in the MongoDB shard in recoverable form.
solution: Revoked the exposed credential, reissued it with least-privilege scope, moved secret storage to a managed service with audited access, and audited remaining credentials for excessive permissions.

issue: 3% of API clients received throttling responses from the pricing engine despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the job scheduler identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the job scheduler so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Database errors affecting the identity service.
root_cause: A schema migration on the ledger table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification. For the window where the index did not exist, queries that depended on it fell back to full scans and saturated the SQLite metadata store.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create.

issue: Sign-in to the partner API failed intermittently while other functionality remained available. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the token validator uses to validate credentials for the document indexer.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. Validation changes are staged behind a per-tenant warning period before they are enforced.

issue: Requests to the ingest gateway failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the ingest gateway. The new default disagreed with the leader elector, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the leader elector cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: The majority of requests to the web dashboard failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A third-party email provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The batch consumer had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Added response validation in the batch consumer so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Credentials held by the entitlement service may have been exposed after a compromise at the upstream CDN.
root_cause: The upstream CDN was itself compromised, and the data it held on behalf of the organisation included access tokens and keys issued for customer integrations with the entitlement service.
solution: Suspended affected integrations immediately, then coordinated with each provider to revoke and reissue every token and key that had been held, rotating internal credentials before resuming service.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the catalogue API in eu-central.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning errors for a subset of requests. The batch consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a downstream KYC vendor. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: New deployments of the audit log writer hung in a pending state for 51 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the audit log writer did not set, so the rate limiter silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the rate limiter to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The document indexer could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in two of three availability zones.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the document indexer did not set, so the config loader silently rejected every new instance. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the ingest gateway did not restore service and left the DynamoDB table in a state neither version could read. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the DynamoDB table, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the DynamoDB table, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Requests to the media transcoder failed across the primary cluster immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the media transcoder started with settings it could not validate. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the media transcoder within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the notification service unable to serve traffic in the primary cluster.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the connection pool still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the primary cluster. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Healthy instances of the notification service were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 6 hours 10 minutes window.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the notification service responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the leader elector expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down.

issue: The reporting UI began returning errors for just under half of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the document indexer itself. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the document indexer started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the document indexer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: A small subset of workers in the ingest gateway became permanently stuck while the process stayed alive.
root_cause: An increase in inbound volume triggered a latent defect in the client library used by the rate limiter, which deadlocked while holding a connection, exhausting the pool without reporting a failure.
solution: Patched the library defect, added a timeout on lock acquisition so a stall surfaces as an error, and added an alert on workers that stop advancing.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the geocoding service did not restore service and left the MongoDB shard in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the MongoDB shard, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the MongoDB shard, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Background jobs in the entitlement service stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of eight thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the audit table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the token validator rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the token validator to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Requests to the recommendation service failed across the primary cluster immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the recommendation service. The new default disagreed with the cache layer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the cache layer cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster.

issue: The chat backend degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the SQLite metadata store was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Batch workloads on the media transcoder ran at reduced throughput for 38 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected. Impact was limited to ca-central.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the messaging bridge, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the messaging bridge failed to reconnect after a restart of the metrics agent and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the webhook dispatcher in the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the sidecar proxy but the webhook dispatcher reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Writes to the devices table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the webhook dispatcher for 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the devices table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Healthy instances of the feed builder were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 14 minutes window.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the feed builder responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the cache layer expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: 63% of payment attempts on the partner API timed out for 51 minutes during a demand surge.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the pricing engine to a downstream KYC vendor became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts.

issue: Users reported the reporting API being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the reporting UI issued one request per item rather than a single batched call.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Errors on the mobile apps following a recent change.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the search API stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the search API actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: The CLI slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the token validator identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. The affected path had no concurrency limit, so a single slow dependency was enough to occupy every available worker.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the token validator so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The document indexer unavailable due to a database fault.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the entitlements table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Background jobs in the geocoding service stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of dozens of thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the session store rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the session store to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The pricing engine could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the pricing engine did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The partner API affected by a security event.
root_cause: A credential with broader permissions than it needed was stored in the Redis cache tier in recoverable form. An attacker who reached the Redis cache tier could therefore pivot into systems unrelated to the original entry point.
solution: Revoked the exposed credential, reissued it with least-privilege scope, moved secret storage to a managed service with audited access, and audited remaining credentials for excessive permissions.

issue: A feature intended for internal testing became active for 24% of customers on the reporting UI without an announcement.
root_cause: A feature flag for the chat backend was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The media transcoder degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the media transcoder did not set, so the sidecar proxy silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the sidecar proxy to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the embedded widget.
root_cause: Session records in the ClickHouse cluster were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the session store.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the sync service made the incident worse and extended impact by 2 hours 5 minutes. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the Redis cache tier in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the sync service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: A small subset of payment attempts on the web dashboard timed out for 51 minutes during a demand surge.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the ingest gateway to an external geolocation API became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts.

issue: Latency on the document indexer was 42% higher in one region for 6 hours 10 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the document indexer in the primary region were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the document indexer at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: Reports generated by the document indexer contained figures that did not reconcile with the underlying records.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the document indexer placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: Latency on the messaging bridge was 55% higher in one region for 23 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the messaging bridge in eu-west were routed to the Cassandra ring in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the messaging bridge at the local replica of the Cassandra ring and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the sync service.
root_cause: A change to the queue infrastructure behind the sync service caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection without raising an error.
solution: Replayed the undelivered callbacks once identified, then added active health checks on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: Access to the public API denied for a subset of users. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the request router caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the request router, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: Writes to the subscriptions table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the feed builder for most of the working day.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the subscriptions table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover.

issue: The webhook dispatcher degraded by a platform-level failure.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The webhook dispatcher called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Recovery required physical intervention, so time to repair was governed by access rather than by diagnosis.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: The messaging bridge degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 63% of queries exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: An index on the webhooks table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the ClickHouse cluster. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal.

issue: Healthy instances of the feed builder were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 1 hour 12 minutes window.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the feed builder responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the token validator expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the webhook dispatcher.
root_cause: The change was tested against a single node but applied to the fleet simultaneously, so a defect that one node could absorb removed capacity everywhere at once. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Reverted the change and introduced staged application across the fleet with a health gate between stages. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: The inventory service timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in eu-west left the inventory service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in eu-west and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the SQLite metadata store in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the export worker failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer.

issue: Read and write errors against the MySQL replica set. Impact was limited to sa-east.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the leader elector selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Credential validation failures in the production fleet.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the queue consumer was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation. Monitoring covered availability of the endpoint rather than successful authentication, so it stayed green.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover. A pre-apply check now lists every resource a policy change will affect before it is applied.

issue: The identity service slowed progressively over 3 hours 20 minutes, with queue depth degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache in front of the DynamoDB table was configured with an expiry short enough that most reads missed. Each miss fell through to the DynamoDB table, so the cache added overhead without absorbing load. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Lengthened the cache expiry to a value matched to how often the underlying data actually changes, which raised the hit rate and returned latency to normal. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: The ingest gateway degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 85% of queries exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: An index on the sessions table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the Redis cache tier.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: 7% of requests to the billing service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning errors for a subset of requests. The metrics agent retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the managed DNS provider.

issue: 63% of requests to the messaging bridge failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The messaging bridge called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Recovery required physical intervention, so time to repair was governed by access rather than by diagnosis.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The document indexer degraded in us-east for 3 hours 20 minutes and automated failover did not fully restore capacity. Impact was limited to us-east.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the document indexer, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down.

issue: Routing for the scheduling service sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting the majority of traffic.
root_cause: An edge configuration set the backend target inside a request handler, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the target to the first entry in the list rather than the intended one. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test that asserts backend selection after a mid-request restart.

issue: 78% of users on the public API saw an unreleased interface for 2 hours 5 minutes before it was withdrawn.
root_cause: A targeting rule meant to match a single internal tenant used a prefix comparison, so it matched a large set of production tenant identifiers that shared the same prefix. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Corrected the targeting rule to an exact-match comparison and added a dry-run report that lists which tenants a rule will match before it is saved.

issue: The document indexer could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in us-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the document indexer did not set, so the cache layer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the cache layer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Reads from the messaging bridge returned stale data for 51 minutes while writes continued to succeed normally. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the DynamoDB table stalled without raising an error.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: A traffic spike on the webhooks endpoint pushed the geocoding service past its capacity and 78% of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the geocoding service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the geocoding service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Read and write errors against the SQLite metadata store.
root_cause: The connection pool for the sync service was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the SQLite metadata store would accept and new connections were refused. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The entitlement service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in sa-east.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the entitlement service did not set, so the cache layer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the cache layer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the chat backend. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the chat backend were dispatched to a neighbouring backend. Retries did not help because the resolution step failed before any connection was attempted.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path.

issue: Errors on the admin console following a recent change.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the metrics agent still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the production fleet. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps.

issue: 94% of requests to the billing service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure. Both the CLI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning errors for a subset of requests. The rate limiter retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a third-party SMS gateway. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: Data access failures in production.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the invoices table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time.

issue: Reduced availability in ap-southeast. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: A node in ap-southeast entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations. The probe tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: All inbound traffic to the reporting API stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the reporting API was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: Authentication requests to the export worker timed out for 18% of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: Session records in the primary Postgres cluster were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the retry handler.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once.

issue: Processing in the pricing engine did not complete as expected.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The pricing engine depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the entitlement service made the incident worse and extended impact by 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the ClickHouse cluster in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the entitlement service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Latency on the entitlement service was 7% higher in one region for 9 hours with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in eu-central left the entitlement service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in eu-central and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: The reporting API could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-northeast.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the reporting API did not set, so the session store silently rejected every new instance. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the session store to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: The pricing engine ran with configuration from the previous release for 14 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the queue consumer but the pricing engine reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: 55% of API clients received throttling responses from the recommendation service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the rate limiter identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the rate limiter so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the webhook dispatcher in all regions.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the admission controller but the webhook dispatcher reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The pricing engine became slow in us-east only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: Instances of the pricing engine in us-east were routed to the SQLite metadata store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the pricing engine at the local replica of the SQLite metadata store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the partner API.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service began returning malformed responses rather than errors.
solution: Added response validation in the admission controller so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: 11% of users could not sign in to the webhooks endpoint for 23 minutes, with no clear pattern by region or account type.
root_cause: A signing key used by the retry handler was rotated without updating every validator, so tokens issued after the rotation were rejected by the services still holding the previous key.
solution: Distributed the new key to all validators and changed rotation to publish the new key and accept both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Background jobs in the search API stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of four thousand items accumulated. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the orders table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the request router rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the request router to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: The admin console affected by a security event. Both the admin console and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A distributed attack saturated the edge capacity serving the admin console. Mitigation rules existed but were scoped to a traffic profile the attack did not match, so they did not engage automatically.
solution: Applied mitigation manually to absorb the attack, then broadened the automatic rules to cover this traffic profile and raised edge capacity headroom.

issue: Latency on the notification service was 78% higher in one region for 9 hours with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the Sydney region left the notification service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in the Sydney region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Payment records inconsistent for a subset of customers.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the request router rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the request router to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: The audit log writer unavailable following a planned change. Impact was limited to us-east.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the audit log writer started with settings it could not validate. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the audit log writer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A handful of API clients received throttling responses from the sync service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the rate limiter identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the rate limiter so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The CLI slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in eu-west were routed to the MongoDB shard in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the MongoDB shard and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The feed builder unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the feed builder was raised past what any node in us-east could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to all regions.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the recommendation service stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the recommendation service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: The search API became unavailable in ap-northeast following a disk failure on a node that continued reporting itself healthy.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the search API failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the media transcoder did not restore service and left the SQLite metadata store in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the SQLite metadata store in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the media transcoder failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The sync service became unreachable for external clients while internal callers were unaffected.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy.

issue: The partner API began returning errors for 31% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the ingest gateway itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the ingest gateway. The new default disagreed with the leader elector, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the leader elector cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: Requests to the reporting API queued and timed out while the Kafka topic itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: The connection pool for the reporting API was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the Kafka topic would accept and new connections were refused. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the inventory service.
root_cause: A retry in the queue consumer re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost. Without an idempotency key, a partner inventory feed treated the retry as a new transaction.
