solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to a partner inventory feed so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: Calls to the webhook dispatcher were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 55% of clients.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the health checker treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing.

issue: 31% of requests to the scheduling service were rejected at the edge while the service itself reported healthy.
root_cause: A filtering rule was changed directly on the edge tier outside the normal pipeline, so the change did not appear in deployment history. Responders spent most of the incident examining recent releases before drift detection surfaced the untracked edit. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band edge change and restricted write access so edits outside the pipeline are blocked, with drift detection alerting on any that still occur.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the identity service.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane experienced a regional fault. The identity service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the managed Kubernetes control plane recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Requests to the webhook dispatcher failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the webhook dispatcher.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the leader elector cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: 85% of requests to the public API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced a regional fault. The search API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Intermittent connection failures in ap-northeast.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the webhook dispatcher was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Queries against the invoices table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the checkout service began timing out for 78% of requests.
root_cause: A schema migration on the invoices table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Replication lag on the ingest gateway rose from normal to several seconds, and 3% of calls to the partner API exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the ingest gateway.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: Batch workloads on the recommendation service ran at reduced throughput for most of the working day while interactive traffic was unaffected.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in ca-central, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region.

issue: Capacity in ap-northeast fell by 42% and the recommendation service began shedding requests.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the recommendation service, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the partner API.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The request router had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Added response validation in the request router so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: 31% of requests to the pricing engine failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning errors for a subset of requests. The request router retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the managed DNS provider.

issue: The sync service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the sync service failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: The chat backend degraded gradually rather than failing outright, and 63% of queries exceeded their timeout. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: An index on the orders table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the Kafka topic. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: 85% of requests to the document indexer were rejected at the edge while the service itself reported healthy.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the document indexer, and the rule applied to the production fleet rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Name lookups for the webhooks endpoint returned errors for 1 hour 12 minutes, with a period of total failure during recovery.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the reporting API still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake.

issue: A scheduled job in the geocoding service did not run for 14 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the geocoding service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur.

issue: Latency on the pricing engine was 55% higher in one region for 2 hours 5 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the Sydney region left the pricing engine running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Restored the instance count in the Sydney region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Calls to the webhook dispatcher were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting a handful of clients.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the config loader identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the config loader so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: 3% of requests to the inventory service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider experienced an outage in us-east. The inventory service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. The redundancy that was expected to cover this failure shared an upstream component with the path that failed.
solution: Served a degraded response while the managed DNS provider recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Read and write errors against the Redis cache tier. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A query plan on the subscriptions table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: Requests to the messaging bridge failed across the primary cluster immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the messaging bridge. The new default disagreed with the request router, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the request router cannot parse before it reaches the primary cluster. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: 55% of API clients received throttling responses from the notification service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the queue consumer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the queue consumer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The document indexer shedding requests under load.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the leader elector identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the leader elector so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The chat backend was degraded for 14 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The chat backend depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the export worker across the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the export worker was raised past what any node in the Sydney region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Single sign-on to the partner API failed for a small subset of enterprise tenants for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the sidecar proxy. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Transaction processing degraded in the entitlement service.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the job scheduler made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Downstream ledger entries were written from the same flow, so the inconsistency propagated into reporting.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the job scheduler to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: The chat backend degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The chat backend depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A small subset of programmatic clients lost access to the partner API without any credential change on their side. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the config loader was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The reporting API briefly ran two active leaders in the primary region, and conflicting writes reached the SQLite metadata store.
root_cause: A lease renewal in the batch consumer was slow enough to let the lease expire while the original holder still believed it was leader.
solution: Added a fencing token so writes from a superseded leader are rejected by the SQLite metadata store, and shortened the renewal interval relative to the lease duration.

issue: The notification service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the notification service did not set, so the retry handler silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the retry handler to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the media transcoder across the production fleet.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the media transcoder stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the media transcoder actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The entitlement service degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the DynamoDB table. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the production fleet.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the export worker. The new default disagreed with the retry handler, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the retry handler cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: New deployments of the recommendation service hung in a pending state for 4 hours 36 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the recommendation service did not set, so the shard mapper silently rejected every new instance. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the shard mapper to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Elevated response times on the reporting UI.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the messaging bridge. As requests queued, client retries added further load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the recommendation service made the incident worse and extended impact by most of the working day.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the MongoDB shard in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the recommendation service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: 24% of payment attempts on the partner API timed out for most of the working day during a demand surge. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The export worker could not scale out to meet the surge because its resource configuration prevented new instances from being placed, even though spare capacity existed.
solution: Corrected the resource configuration so instances could be scheduled onto available capacity, and added load testing ahead of promotional events to surface scaling limits in advance.

issue: Latency on the reporting API was 7% higher in one region for 1 hour 12 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the reporting API in eu-west were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the reporting API at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Queries against the audit table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the webhook dispatcher began timing out for 3% of requests.
root_cause: A schema migration on the audit table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The web dashboard slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: A cache key for the notification service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the primary Postgres cluster. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Requests to the document indexer failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the document indexer. The new default disagreed with the connection pool, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the connection pool cannot parse before it reaches production.

issue: A migration on the events table that had run cleanly for weeks caused a sharp availability drop in its final step. Both the public API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the events table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together. The query planner had no recent statistics for the affected relation, so it continued choosing a plan that no longer suited the data.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: New deployments of the pricing engine hung in a pending state for 23 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the pricing engine did not set, so the metrics agent silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the metrics agent to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the pricing engine in the production fleet.

solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the pricing engine actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

solution: Restored the instance count in sa-east and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The feed builder exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected 7% of requests.
root_cause: The connection pool for the feed builder was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the time-series store would accept and new connections were refused.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value.

issue: The ingest gateway stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 38 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the request router rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the request router to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Elevated query latency against the time-series store.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the cache layer selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty.

issue: API tokens for the webhook dispatcher were rejected as invalid for 23 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the MySQL replica set did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the config loader could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the MySQL replica set and changed the config loader to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: Callers of the media transcoder saw response times multiply for 6 hours 10 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The leader elector began synchronously calling a third-party email provider on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to a third-party email provider back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Requests to the admin console failed TLS negotiation for a handful of clients starting at a fixed time of day. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the media transcoder expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Retries did not help because the resolution step failed before any connection was attempted.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: API tokens for the media transcoder were rejected as invalid for 1 hour 47 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the time-series store did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the retry handler could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. Because tokens are cached by clients, the impact appeared gradually as existing tokens expired.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the time-series store and changed the retry handler to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: Credential validation failures in the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A signing key used by the config loader was rotated without updating every validator, so tokens issued after the rotation were rejected by the services still holding the previous key. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Distributed the new key to all validators and changed rotation to publish the new key and accept both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the metrics agent still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the shared staging-to-production path. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps.

issue: Work assigned to one node in two of three availability zones stalled for 38 minutes while the node remained in rotation.
root_cause: A node in two of three availability zones entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: New deployments of the chat backend hung in a pending state for 2 hours 5 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the chat backend did not set, so the rate limiter silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the rate limiter to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: The feed builder was degraded for most of the working day because of a fault at a third-party email provider rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A third-party email provider experienced a regional fault. The feed builder depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party email provider recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The media transcoder degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and request throughput on the Cassandra ring rose steadily for 2 hours 5 minutes. Both the reporting UI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A new query against the webhooks table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the Cassandra ring. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The mobile apps displayed incorrect values to the majority of users for 4 hours 36 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the export worker placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records.

issue: The feed builder returned elevated errors for 38 minutes after a sudden increase in inbound volume.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the feed builder had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete. Queues grew past the queue depth limit and requests began failing after already consuming capacity. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Added admission control so the feed builder rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: The checkout service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the admission controller still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the production fleet. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted.

issue: The embedded widget began returning errors for 24% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the chat backend itself.

The system correctly protected interactive requests, which meant sustained degradation for batch work until both activities completed. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region.

issue: Errors on the CLI following a recent change.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the ingest gateway was raised past what any node in us-east could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Reduced availability in the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service began returning errors for a subset of requests. The batch consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the cloud provider block-storage service.

issue: Authentication requests to the webhook dispatcher timed out for roughly a third of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: Session records in the MongoDB shard were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the connection pool.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Healthy instances of the audit log writer were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 14 minutes window.

The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the admission controller expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The messaging bridge was degraded for 51 minutes because of a fault at a third-party SMS gateway rather than in the organisation's own systems.

Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The ingest gateway became slow in ca-central only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in ca-central were routed to the MongoDB shard in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the MongoDB shard and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The asset pipeline affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the asset pipeline failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: The feed builder unavailable due to a database fault.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the orders table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced. Once the referenced values exceeded the narrower range, every insert failed with an overflow. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: 94% of requests to the mobile apps failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The feed builder depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A low-risk change to the production fleet resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the production fleet was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly.

issue: A small subset of users on the webhooks endpoint saw an unreleased interface for 14 minutes before it was withdrawn. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A feature flag for the media transcoder was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The messaging bridge ran with configuration from the previous release for 6 hours 10 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the config loader but the messaging bridge reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The audit log writer returned elevated errors for 2 hours 5 minutes after a sudden increase in inbound volume. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the audit log writer had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete. Queues grew past the file-descriptor limit and requests began failing after already consuming capacity.
solution: Added admission control so the audit log writer rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the webhook dispatcher did not restore service and left the Redis cache tier in a state neither version could read. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Redis cache tier, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Redis cache tier, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Security incident affecting the export worker.
root_cause: A credential with broader permissions than it needed was stored in the Cassandra ring in recoverable form.
solution: Revoked the exposed credential, reissued it with least-privilege scope, moved secret storage to a managed service with audited access, and audited remaining credentials for excessive permissions.

issue: Queries against the orders table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the asset pipeline began timing out for 24% of requests. Impact was limited to the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: A schema migration on the orders table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Sign-in and authorisation errors on the SDK.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the shard mapper uses to validate credentials for the recommendation service.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: The audit log writer degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the audit log writer. The new default disagreed with the admission controller, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the admission controller cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: 18% of requests to the export worker failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning errors for a subset of requests. The queue consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the upstream CDN.

issue: The messaging bridge was removed from rotation in us-east despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 55%.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The MongoDB shard became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the MongoDB shard.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The document indexer stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the orders table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the connection pool rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the connection pool to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the reporting UI.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the metrics agent was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: Replication lag on the reporting API rose from normal to several seconds, and 94% of calls to the webhooks endpoint exceeded their timeout.
root_cause: The metrics agent began synchronously calling the upstream CDN on a path that had previously been asynchronous. Each request inherited the dependency latency, and the thread pool filled with waiting work.
solution: Moved the call to the upstream CDN back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Sign-in to the reporting UI failed intermittently while other functionality remained available.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the token validator uses to validate credentials for the chat backend. Because the failure was in the credential path rather than the application, every feature behind sign-in became unreachable.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect.

issue: The billing service was degraded for 23 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The billing service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. issue: The checkout service ran with configuration from the previous release for 38 minutes even though the deploy reported success. Both the partner API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the checkout service stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the checkout service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The ingest gateway stalled with no errors reported.
root_cause: The token validator read a value, computed a new one and wrote it back without a transaction or compare-and-set. Concurrent requests for the same record interleaved between the read and the write, so one update silently overwrote the other.
solution: Repaired the affected records and changed the update to a single conditional write so a concurrent modification fails and retries rather than being lost.

issue: 3% of API responses from the document indexer could return records belonging to another tenant.
root_cause: A large change was labelled internally as a routine update and received far less review than its scope warranted. It removed a tenant filter from a query path in the document indexer, so results were no longer scoped to the caller. Because the credential had broader permissions than it needed, the reachable surface was far larger than the initial entry point.
solution: Reverted the change, audited access logs for cross-tenant reads, and introduced risk-proportional review requirements so a change of that size cannot be labelled routine.

issue: The audit log writer failed to start in eu-central after a dependency upgrade, and 42% of requests to the CLI returned errors.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The leader elector had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the leader elector to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Requests to the billing service failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the billing service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the billing service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the ingest gateway made the incident worse and extended impact by 14 minutes. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the object store bucket in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the ingest gateway failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: A scheduled job in the billing service did not run for 4 hours 36 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the billing service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: The entitlement service failed to start in eu-central after a dependency upgrade, and 18% of requests to the embedded widget returned errors.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the token validator still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in a single production cell. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: 11% of requests to the webhooks endpoint failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The rate limiter had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Added response validation in the rate limiter so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The billing service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-southeast.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the billing service was raised past what any node in ap-southeast could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Payment records inconsistent for a subset of customers. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The chat backend could not scale out to meet the surge because its resource configuration prevented new instances from being placed, even though spare capacity existed.
solution: Corrected the resource configuration so instances could be scheduled onto available capacity, and added load testing ahead of promotional events to surface scaling limits in advance. Active health checks were added on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: Work assigned to one node in eu-central stalled for 1 hour 47 minutes while the node remained in rotation.
root_cause: A node in eu-central entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: The identity service was degraded for 9 hours because of a fault at the cloud provider block-storage service rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The identity service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 3 hours 20 minutes, while the payments themselves completed normally.
root_cause: A change to the queue infrastructure behind the chat backend caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection without raising an error.
solution: Replayed the undelivered callbacks once identified, then added active health checks on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: The billing service became slow in ap-southeast only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in ap-southeast left the billing service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Restored the instance count in ap-southeast and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: The webhook dispatcher degraded after a routine rollout.
