root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced an outage in the Sydney region. The billing service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one.
solution: Served a degraded response while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The billing service availability fell by 55% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the audit table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the export worker in the primary cluster. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the serialisation layer but the export worker reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete.

issue: The notification service slowed progressively over 2 hours 5 minutes, with p99 latency degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache key for the notification service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the MySQL replica set.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting.

issue: The SDK began returning errors for 11% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the billing service itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the billing service. The new default disagreed with the health checker, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the health checker cannot parse before it reaches production. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: The catalogue API degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the catalogue API did not set, so the sidecar proxy silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the sidecar proxy to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Healthy instances of the feed builder were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 38 minutes window.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the feed builder responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the config loader expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: A power interruption took the production fleet offline and recovery took considerably longer than planned.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the asset pipeline were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths.

issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 9 hours, while the payments themselves completed normally.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the serialisation layer made some callback payloads unencodable.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the serialisation layer to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: Requests to the reporting API failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the reporting API. The new default disagreed with the metrics agent, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the metrics agent cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: Calls to the checkout service were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 31% of clients. Both the embedded widget and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the admission controller identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the admission controller so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the admin console. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A rounding change in the leader elector was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. A cached fallback and status indicator were added so an upstream fault degrades the feature rather than removing it.

issue: The Redis cache tier became unreachable and recovery required restoring from an older snapshot than expected.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the Redis cache tier. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the export worker in the primary cluster.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the token validator but the export worker reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to all regions.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the checkout service started with settings it could not validate. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the checkout service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The catalogue API stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 9 hours.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the events table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the queue consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the queue consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the ingest gateway in all regions.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the connection pool but the ingest gateway reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Four hundred payments were double-counted in the sessions table before the discrepancy was detected.
root_cause: A failover of the object store bucket mid-transaction left a partial record. The reconciliation job treated the partial row as missing and re-submitted it, producing a duplicate.
solution: Reversed the duplicates, and changed reconciliation to resolve a partial record against the processor's ledger before re-submitting anything.

issue: Errors on the public API following a recent change. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the messaging bridge stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the messaging bridge actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: 3% of users on the webhooks endpoint saw an unreleased interface for 4 hours 36 minutes before it was withdrawn.
root_cause: A feature flag for the geocoding service was created with a default-on value rather than default-off. The flag service treats an absent per-tenant override as the default, so every tenant without an explicit override received the new behaviour.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the inventory service made the incident worse and extended impact by 9 hours. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the SQLite metadata store in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the inventory service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: The CLI began returning errors for 3% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the search API itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the search API. The new default disagreed with the job scheduler, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the job scheduler cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: All inbound traffic to the identity service stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect production to the outside world.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane.

issue: The web dashboard became slow for 11% of users while backend services reported normal p99 latency.
root_cause: A client-side change in the web dashboard issued one request per item rather than a single batched call.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: 11% of requests to the recommendation service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced an outage in the Frankfurt region. The recommendation service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one.
solution: Served a degraded response while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in sa-east.
root_cause: Instances of the pricing engine in sa-east were routed to the SQLite metadata store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the pricing engine at the local replica of the SQLite metadata store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: A scheduled job in the billing service did not run for 23 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the ClickHouse cluster was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying. Because every internal component reported healthy, responders spent much of the incident ruling out their own systems.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: Single sign-on to the partner API failed for 85% of enterprise tenants for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the serialisation layer caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the serialisation layer, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: Unauthorised activity detected in the primary cluster.
root_cause: A caching layer added in front of the feed builder keyed entries without the tenant identifier, so a response generated for one tenant could be served to another. Because the credential had broader permissions than it needed, the reachable surface was far larger than the initial entry point.
solution: Added the tenant identifier to the cache key, invalidated the cache entirely, and added a test asserting that a response generated for one tenant is never served to another.

issue: The embedded widget began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the document indexer itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the document indexer. The new default disagreed with the session store, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the session store cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the scheduling service.
root_cause: The change was tested against a single node but applied to the fleet simultaneously, so a defect that one node could absorb removed capacity everywhere at once. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Reverted the change and introduced staged application across the fleet with a health gate between stages. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: The SDK began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the ingest gateway itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the ingest gateway started with settings it could not validate. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the ingest gateway within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The messaging bridge affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced an outage in us-west. The messaging bridge called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Served a degraded response while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Payment failures affecting the embedded widget. Impact was limited to sa-east.
root_cause: The recommendation service could not scale out to meet the surge because its resource configuration prevented new instances from being placed, even though spare capacity existed. Incoming payment requests queued and began exceeding their deadline.
solution: Corrected the resource configuration so instances could be scheduled onto available capacity, and added load testing ahead of promotional events to surface scaling limits in advance.

issue: Requests to the checkout service failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the checkout service. The new default disagreed with the shard mapper, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the shard mapper cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: New deployments of the chat backend hung in a pending state for 38 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the chat backend did not set, so the leader elector silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the leader elector to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: A subset of transactions in the messaging bridge were recorded twice over a most of the working day window.
root_cause: A retry in the request router re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to a third-party SMS gateway so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: Elevated response times on the mobile apps.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the sync service. As requests queued, client retries added further load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client.

issue: The messaging bridge availability fell by 24% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the primary Postgres cluster. The affected replicas entered recovery, which pushed their load onto the remainder and cascaded into a broader capacity shortfall.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Credential validation failures in the primary cluster.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the ClickHouse cluster did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the leader elector could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the ClickHouse cluster and changed the leader elector to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: The admin console began returning errors for 94% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the asset pipeline itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the asset pipeline. The new default disagreed with the config loader, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the config loader cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: The entitlement service availability fell by 24% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the SQLite metadata store. The affected replicas entered recovery, which pushed their load onto the remainder and cascaded into a broader capacity shortfall. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: 31% of requests to the web dashboard were served by an unintended backend for 1 hour 12 minutes. Impact was limited to eu-west.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the identity service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Name lookups for the reporting UI returned errors for 51 minutes, with a period of total failure during recovery.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the catalogue API still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake.

issue: Authentication requests to the export worker timed out for 85% of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: Session records in the MongoDB shard were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the sidecar proxy.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once. A pre-apply check now lists every resource a policy change will affect before it is applied.

issue: The public API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the queue consumer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the queue consumer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Work assigned to one node in eu-central stalled for 4 hours 36 minutes while the node remained in rotation. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the scheduling service failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete. Recovery required physical intervention, so time to repair was governed by access rather than by diagnosis.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The catalogue API unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the catalogue API did not set, so the metrics agent silently rejected every new instance. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the metrics agent to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Internal name resolution failed across the production fleet and services could no longer reach one another for 6 hours 10 minutes. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the feed builder and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock.

issue: The webhook dispatcher unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the webhook dispatcher was raised past what any node in the primary region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: 18% of requests to the ingest gateway failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in eu-west. The ingest gateway called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. Nominally redundant paths were audited for shared upstream components and separated where they were not independent.

issue: A small subset of requests to the embedded widget were served by an unintended backend for 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: An edge configuration set the backend target inside a request handler, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the target to the first entry in the list rather than the intended one. The change looked routine in review because its effect depended on which resolver path a caller happened to use.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test that asserts backend selection after a mid-request restart. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: Elevated response times on the SDK.
root_cause: Instances of the ingest gateway in eu-central were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the ingest gateway at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the identity service across the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the identity service. The new default disagreed with the rate limiter, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the rate limiter cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: The ingest gateway was degraded for 23 minutes because of a fault at a partner inventory feed rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced a regional fault. The ingest gateway depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the entitlement service across production.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the entitlement service did not set, so the connection pool silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the connection pool to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Network errors between services in the production fleet. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the document indexer failed to reconnect after a restart of the retry handler and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. Certificate and record expiry are now alerted well before the deadline rather than reported silently.

issue: Requests to the media transcoder failed across a single production cell immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the media transcoder. The new default disagreed with the metrics agent, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the metrics agent cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The document indexer was unavailable for 4 hours 36 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the primary Postgres cluster. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The web dashboard unreachable for a subset of clients.
root_cause: A script restarted only the authoritative resolver after an address change and left the caching resolver untouched, so cached lookups began timing out. The subsequent repair rebuilt the zone using a tool that itself depended on working DNS, producing a zone that returned not-found for many names. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Rebuilt and republished a correct zone by hand, restarted both resolvers, and added a rule that DNS-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a DNS outage.

issue: The CLI displayed incorrect values to 63% of users for 23 minutes while every service reported healthy. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A rounding change in the shard mapper was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the checkout service.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the Elasticsearch index did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the token validator could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the Elasticsearch index and changed the token validator to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the webhook dispatcher.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect the shared staging-to-production path to the outside world. The same change removed the paths engineers would have used to reach the equipment remotely.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: The entitlement service degraded by a platform-level failure.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the entitlement service were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths.

issue: Reads from the messaging bridge returned stale data for most of the working day while writes continued to succeed normally.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Kafka topic, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Batch workloads on the recommendation service ran at reduced throughput for 1 hour 47 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in ap-southeast, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes. The system correctly protected interactive requests, which meant sustained degradation for batch work until both activities completed.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: The ingest gateway degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and cache hit rate on the Redis cache tier rose steadily for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A new query against the documents table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the Redis cache tier.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the audit log writer. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the health checker rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the health checker to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: The scheduling service degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and replication lag on the ClickHouse cluster rose steadily for 1 hour 12 minutes.
root_cause: A schema migration on the sessions table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification. For the window where the index did not exist, queries that depended on it fell back to full scans and saturated the ClickHouse cluster.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Database errors affecting the scheduling service.
root_cause: The connection pool for the scheduling service was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the DynamoDB table would accept and new connections were refused. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: A change to the reporting API introduced a flaw that allowed data to be read across tenant boundaries.
root_cause: A large change was labelled internally as a routine update and received far less review than its scope warranted.
solution: Reverted the change, audited access logs for cross-tenant reads, and introduced risk-proportional review requirements so a change of that size cannot be labelled routine.

issue: Checkout on the web dashboard failed for 85% of attempts during a promotional traffic peak. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the messaging bridge to an upstream payment processor became the bottleneck under peak load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts. Active health checks were added on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: The reporting API was unavailable for 9 hours and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the Cassandra ring.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The messaging bridge could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in the primary region.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the messaging bridge did not set, so the batch consumer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the batch consumer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: A forgotten system retained access to the primary cluster and was used to reach production data.
root_cause: A host removed from active service retained its network access and service account. Nothing reconciled the inventory against issued credentials, so the stale access went unnoticed.
solution: Revoked the stale access and added periodic reconciliation between the host inventory and issued credentials so orphaned access is detected automatically. A decommissioning process was introduced that revokes credentials and network access as part of retirement.

issue: Requests to the reporting API failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the reporting API started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the reporting API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The feed builder degraded by a platform-level failure. Impact was limited to the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in the Frankfurt region below what was needed to serve normal traffic. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the shortfall.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Roughly a third of API clients received throttling responses from the checkout service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the sidecar proxy identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the sidecar proxy so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The feed builder was degraded for 4 hours 36 minutes because of a fault at an external geolocation API rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An external geolocation API began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The retry handler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Added response validation in the retry handler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the checkout service did not restore service and left the Cassandra ring in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Cassandra ring, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Cassandra ring, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Users reported the asset pipeline being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the SDK issued one request per item rather than a single batched call.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: The notification service slowed progressively over 51 minutes, with connection count degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache key for the notification service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the SQLite metadata store.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting.

issue: A feature intended for internal testing became active for 3% of customers on the partner API without an announcement.
root_cause: A feature flag for the sync service was created with a default-on value rather than default-off. The flag service treats an absent per-tenant override as the default, so every tenant without an explicit override received the new behaviour.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time.

issue: 7% of reads served by the export worker reflected data minutes behind the primary. Impact was limited to two of three availability zones.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the Cassandra ring stalled without raising an error. Monitoring tracked replica availability but not replication lag, so the stall was invisible until customers reported inconsistency.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Requests to the chat backend failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the chat backend started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the chat backend within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: New deployments of the search API hung in a pending state for 1 hour 12 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the search API was raised past what any node in the Sydney region could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region.

issue: Traffic to the feed builder failing to reach its destination.
root_cause: A script restarted only the authoritative resolver after an address change and left the caching resolver untouched, so cached lookups began timing out. The subsequent repair rebuilt the zone using a tool that itself depended on working DNS, producing a zone that returned not-found for many names.
solution: Rebuilt and republished a correct zone by hand, restarted both resolvers, and added a rule that DNS-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a DNS outage.

issue: Elevated query latency against the Kafka topic.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the webhooks table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the batch consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the batch consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The identity service degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: An index on the documents table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the object store bucket.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the admin console was blocked for 51 minutes with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the media transcoder, and the rule applied to all regions rather than a single tenant. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The public API displayed incorrect values to 85% of users for 14 minutes while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the entitlement service placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Errors on the admin console following a recent change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the shared staging-to-production path because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the feed builder started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the feed builder within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Unauthorised activity detected in all regions.
root_cause: A host removed from active service retained its network access and service account. Nothing reconciled the inventory against issued credentials, so the stale access went unnoticed. Because the access used valid credentials, it did not trigger any of the anomaly rules that were in place.
solution: Revoked the stale access and added periodic reconciliation between the host inventory and issued credentials so orphaned access is detected automatically.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the webhook dispatcher in the primary cluster. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the webhook dispatcher stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the webhook dispatcher actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Intermittent connection failures in sa-east.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the export worker and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty. Everything that depended on that name began failing resolution.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: Users were unable to sign in or load the reporting UI platform-wide, with error rates climbing for 3 hours 20 minutes.
root_cause: Session records in the MongoDB shard were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the shard mapper. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: The SDK unreachable for a subset of clients.
root_cause: A zone update removed a record set that the scheduling service still relied on. Negative responses were cached downstream, so the failure persisted after the record was restored. Because service discovery itself was affected, healthy instances could not be found and traffic continued to reach replaced ones.
solution: Restored the record set and shortened the negative-response cache lifetime so a corrected record propagates promptly after a mistake. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: The inventory service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the inventory service did not set, so the config loader silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Background jobs in the audit log writer stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of six thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the invoices table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the config loader rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the config loader to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The majority of requests to the partner API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced a regional fault. The entitlement service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: A small subset of API clients received throttling responses from the document indexer despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the cache layer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the cache layer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The inventory service could not create new records, returning a database-level error unrelated to any application change.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the orders table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover.

issue: Federated login to the identity service broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the job scheduler caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the job scheduler, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: The document indexer was degraded for 6 hours 10 minutes because of a fault at an external geolocation API rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: An external geolocation API began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The retry handler had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The absence of an expected event produced no signal, since alerting covered failures rather than omissions.
solution: Added response validation in the retry handler so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: New deployments of the feed builder hung in a pending state for most of the working day, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the feed builder did not set, so the retry handler silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the retry handler to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Database errors affecting the ingest gateway.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the webhooks table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: 42% of requests to the web dashboard failed while every internal component reported healthy. Both the web dashboard and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor experienced a regional fault. The asset pipeline depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an upstream payment processor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. Dead-man alerting was added so an expected run that does not occur produces a signal.

issue: Latency on the ingest gateway was 24% higher in one region for 1 hour 12 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in two of three availability zones left the ingest gateway running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in two of three availability zones and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to all regions.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the feed builder started with settings it could not validate. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the feed builder within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the search API. Impact was limited to eu-central.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in eu-central left the search API running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in eu-central and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Latency on the sync service was 11% higher in one region for 1 hour 47 minutes with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the sync service in sa-east were routed to the ClickHouse cluster in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Repointed the sync service at the local replica of the ClickHouse cluster and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Lower-priority processing in ap-southeast was delayed by most of the working day during planned maintenance.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. Recovery required physical intervention, so time to repair was governed by access rather than by diagnosis.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: 7% of merchants did not receive delivery callbacks from the billing service and were unaware of completed transactions.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the rate limiter made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Downstream ledger entries were written from the same flow, so the inconsistency propagated into reporting.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the rate limiter to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: The entitlement service became slow in the Frankfurt region only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in the Frankfurt region left the entitlement service running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in the Frankfurt region and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Work assigned to one node in the Sydney region stalled for 2 hours 5 minutes while the node remained in rotation. Both the admin console and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the notification service failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: New deployments of the sync service hung in a pending state for 6 hours 10 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the sync service did not set, so the batch consumer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the batch consumer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The chat backend degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: An external geolocation API experienced a regional fault. The chat backend depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an external geolocation API recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The checkout service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the checkout service. The new default disagreed with the serialisation layer, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the serialisation layer cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Requests to the media transcoder failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. Both the CLI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the media transcoder. The new default disagreed with the rate limiter, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the rate limiter cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: The web dashboard began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the feed builder itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the feed builder. The new default disagreed with the job scheduler, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the job scheduler cannot parse before it reaches production.

issue: Requests to the asset pipeline failed across a single production cell immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the asset pipeline. The new default disagreed with the rate limiter, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the rate limiter cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: A scheduled job in the webhook dispatcher did not run for 1 hour 12 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the webhook dispatcher was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur.

issue: Errors on the partner API following a recent change.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the identity service was raised past what any node in ca-central could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: The pricing engine degraded for a subset of users.
root_cause: A rounding change in the queue consumer was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

issue: Replication lag on the Elasticsearch index rose steadily over 2 hours 5 minutes and the pricing engine began shedding requests, with no change in traffic volume.
root_cause: A query plan on the invoices table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again.

issue: Reduced availability in ap-southeast. Impact was limited to ap-southeast.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting production was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.
