root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the messaging bridge placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The chat backend degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the ClickHouse cluster stalled without raising an error.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The scheduling service was offline for most of the working day after a power event at the facility hosting the primary cluster.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting the primary cluster was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed. Key details of the provider's failover arrangement had not been documented in advance, which slowed diagnosis.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events.

issue: 18% of requests from the recommendation service were sent to instances that no longer existed. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A static routing configuration had not kept pace with infrastructure growth, so updated discovery information could not reach every consumer. Clients continued working from a stale view and sent traffic to instances that had been replaced. Internal callers were affected while external monitoring continued to pass, so detection relied on customer reports.
solution: Restored discovery data to the affected consumers and changed the routing configuration to scale with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Processing in the notification service did not complete as expected. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the primary cluster was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: The recommendation service silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the devices table without updates. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the recommendation service was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the sync service made the incident worse and extended impact by 4 hours 36 minutes.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the Cassandra ring, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the Cassandra ring, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The public API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the serialisation layer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the serialisation layer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: 42% of requests to the scheduling service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The upstream CDN experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The scheduling service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Served a degraded response while the upstream CDN recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The asset pipeline timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the asset pipeline for every caller. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: Authentication requests to the scheduling service timed out for 18% of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the MySQL replica set past what it could serve. The automated protective throttle was initially tuned too aggressively and had to be corrected in smaller steps.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions.

issue: Requests to the asset pipeline failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. Impact was limited to the primary region.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the asset pipeline started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the asset pipeline within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The notification service became slow in ap-southeast only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: Instances of the notification service in ap-southeast were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the notification service at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Reduced availability in the primary region.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts.

issue: The reporting API became unreachable for external clients while internal callers were unaffected.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy.

issue: A maintenance window on the primary cluster that was expected to be routine caused 4 hours 36 minutes of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the primary cluster was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly.

issue: The identity service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in the Sydney region. The identity service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. The redundancy that was expected to cover this failure shared an upstream component with the path that failed.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The webhook dispatcher was degraded for 1 hour 12 minutes because of a fault at a partner inventory feed rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced a regional fault. The webhook dispatcher depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because every internal component reported healthy, responders spent much of the incident ruling out their own systems.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A traffic spike on the reporting UI pushed the document indexer past its capacity and 94% of requests failed.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the document indexer for every caller. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: The checkout service returned elevated errors for 9 hours after a sudden increase in inbound volume.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the checkout service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the checkout service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: New deployments of the sync service hung in a pending state for 4 hours 36 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the sync service did not set, so the batch consumer silently rejected every new instance. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the batch consumer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Nodes running the webhook dispatcher restarted repeatedly on out-of-memory conditions, and cluster leadership moved between them.
root_cause: A background agent on each node retried a failing call to an upstream payment processor in a loop, retaining the context of every attempt. Under sustained load the retained contexts exhausted available memory and the node was terminated.
solution: Bounded the retry loop and released the context between attempts, then added alerting specific to this agent's memory use since the node's normal dynamic usage had masked the growth.

issue: Errors on the partner API following a recent change.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the chat backend responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the request router expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down.

issue: Data access failures in all regions. Impact was limited to ca-central.
root_cause: A new query against the devices table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the Kafka topic. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Requests to the document indexer queued and timed out while the Redis cache tier itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the thread-pool bound well below the load it had previously handled. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion.

issue: API tokens for the media transcoder were rejected as invalid for 51 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the MongoDB shard did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the job scheduler could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the MongoDB shard and changed the job scheduler to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: The inventory service unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: An edge configuration set the backend target inside a request handler, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the target to the first entry in the list rather than the intended one. Every service that resolved the affected name failed together, which made the blast radius far larger than the change implied.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test that asserts backend selection after a mid-request restart.

issue: Roughly a third of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the recommendation service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock.

issue: The identity service degraded after a routine rollout. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The serialisation layer had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the serialisation layer to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: The reporting UI began returning errors for just under half of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the reporting API itself. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the reporting API started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the reporting API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The search API was degraded for 1 hour 47 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The sidecar proxy had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Added response validation in the sidecar proxy so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Batch workloads on the audit log writer ran at reduced throughput for most of the working day while interactive traffic was unaffected.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in sa-east, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A subset of transactions in the ingest gateway were recorded twice over a 4 hours 36 minutes window.
root_cause: A failover of the object store bucket mid-transaction left a partial record. The reconciliation job treated the partial row as missing and re-submitted it, producing a duplicate. Alerting was keyed on error rate rather than on completion rate, so a silent stall produced no signal.
solution: Reversed the duplicates, and changed reconciliation to resolve a partial record against the processor's ledger before re-submitting anything.

issue: The catalogue API could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in us-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the catalogue API did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Just under half of requests to the ingest gateway failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor experienced an outage in ap-southeast. The ingest gateway called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. The fault was intermittent, so instances were repeatedly returned to service before being removed for good.
solution: Served a degraded response while an upstream payment processor recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: The inventory service slowed progressively over 4 hours 36 minutes, with p99 latency degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache key for the inventory service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the Kafka topic.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Elevated response times on the web dashboard.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the serialisation layer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. As queues grew, client retries added load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the serialisation layer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. A capacity model was built from measured dependency latency and is reviewed before each peak event.

issue: Requests to the search API failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. Both the admin console and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the search API started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the search API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the public API. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the MySQL replica set did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the cache layer could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. Monitoring covered availability of the endpoint rather than successful authentication, so it stayed green.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the MySQL replica set and changed the cache layer to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the search API.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the metrics agent rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field. Those payouts were queued rather than failed, so they accumulated silently until the delay was noticed. Merchants had no way to distinguish a delayed payment from a failed one, which generated substantial support load.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the metrics agent to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue.

issue: The sync service was unavailable for 51 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the DynamoDB table.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure.

issue: The catalogue API was degraded for 1 hour 47 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The token validator had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Added response validation in the token validator so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The reporting API became slow in sa-east only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: Instances of the reporting API in sa-east were routed to the MySQL replica set in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the reporting API at the local replica of the MySQL replica set and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: The recommendation service degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and queue depth on the MongoDB shard rose steadily for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A schema migration on the events table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification. For the window where the index did not exist, queries that depended on it fell back to full scans and saturated the MongoDB shard. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: A new code path in the entitlement service caused intermittent hangs and crashes that could not be reproduced reliably.
root_cause: Shared state in the health checker was accessed without synchronisation from a callback that could run on a different thread, so corruption appeared only when the callback overlapped with a request.
solution: Confined the shared state behind a single owner and added a race detector to the test pipeline so this class of defect fails the build.

issue: Background jobs in the ingest gateway stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of several hundred thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the sessions table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the admission controller rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the admission controller to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: All inbound traffic to the notification service stopped and remote management tooling was also unreachable.
root_cause: A routing policy change intended to assess available capacity withdrew the routes that connect a single production cell to the outside world.
solution: Restored the routing configuration through out-of-band access, which required physical presence at the facility, then added a separate management path that does not depend on the production routing plane.

issue: 55% of programmatic clients lost access to the partner API without any credential change on their side.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the Elasticsearch index did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the job scheduler could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the Elasticsearch index and changed the job scheduler to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: New deployments of the checkout service hung in a pending state for 14 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the checkout service did not set, so the batch consumer silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the batch consumer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the search API unable to serve traffic in production. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the shard mapper still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in production. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change. Both the web dashboard and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A targeting rule meant to match a single internal tenant used a prefix comparison, so it matched a large set of production tenant identifiers that shared the same prefix. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Corrected the targeting rule to an exact-match comparison and added a dry-run report that lists which tenants a rule will match before it is saved.

issue: The geocoding service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 38 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the batch consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the batch consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Calls to the catalogue API were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 24% of clients.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the shard mapper identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the shard mapper so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Roughly a third of users could not sign in to the web dashboard for 2 hours 5 minutes, with no clear pattern by region or account type.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the session store uses to validate credentials for the checkout service. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: Latency on the SDK crept upward across the day with no corresponding rise in traffic.
root_cause: A cache key for the entitlement service included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the MongoDB shard. Autoscaling keyed on CPU rather than queue depth, so it did not add capacity while requests were waiting rather than computing.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting.

issue: The asset pipeline could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-west. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the asset pipeline did not set, so the config loader silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Production lost external connectivity for 1 hour 12 minutes, including the remote access paths needed to diagnose the problem. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the export worker was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges.

issue: The webhooks endpoint displayed incorrect values to 31% of users for 23 minutes while every service reported healthy. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A rounding change in the session store was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the search API. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the search API expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the catalogue API in the Frankfurt region. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A node in the Frankfurt region entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations. The probe tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. Health checks were extended to exercise a real operation so a component that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: The entitlement service became unreachable for external clients while internal callers were unaffected.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded. Internal callers were affected while external monitoring continued to pass, so detection relied on customer reports.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Delays in payment processing through the notification service.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the shard mapper made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Alerting was keyed on error rate rather than on completion rate, so a silent stall produced no signal.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the shard mapper to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the document indexer made the incident worse and extended impact by 6 hours 10 minutes.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the Elasticsearch index in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the document indexer failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer.

issue: The inventory service degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the batch consumer still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in all regions. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Requests to the ingest gateway failed across a single production cell immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the ingest gateway. The new default disagreed with the admission controller, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the admission controller cannot parse before it reaches a single production cell.

issue: Payouts from the asset pipeline were delayed by 23 minutes for 42% of recipients. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A timezone change in the scheduling configuration for the asset pipeline moved the payout cutoff past the window during which a partner inventory feed accepts same-day instructions, so batches were held until the next cycle. Reconciliation ran only daily, so the discrepancy was not surfaced until well after the window closed.
solution: Restored the scheduling configuration to the correct timezone and pinned the cutoff to the processor's stated window rather than a local time. Completion rate is now alerted alongside error rate so a silent stall produces a signal.

issue: 78% of requests to the catalogue API failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane began returning errors for a subset of requests. The request router retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Because the component reported itself healthy, the orchestrator kept scheduling work onto it that could not complete.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the managed Kubernetes control plane.

issue: A small subset of requests from the billing service were sent to instances that no longer existed.
root_cause: A static routing configuration had not kept pace with infrastructure growth, so updated discovery information could not reach every consumer.
solution: Restored discovery data to the affected consumers and changed the routing configuration to scale with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: The pricing engine was degraded for 1 hour 47 minutes because of an outage at the managed Kubernetes control plane.
root_cause: The managed Kubernetes control plane began returning errors for a subset of requests. The queue consumer retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the managed Kubernetes control plane.

issue: The media transcoder could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-northeast.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the media transcoder did not set, so the leader elector silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the leader elector to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the asset pipeline started with settings it could not validate. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the asset pipeline within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Requests to the chat backend failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to production because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the chat backend started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the chat backend within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the export worker across the primary cluster.
root_cause: A feature flag for the export worker was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: 85% of requests to the web dashboard were served by an unintended backend for 1 hour 47 minutes.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the feed builder were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: The geocoding service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 3 hours 20 minutes. Both the partner API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the request router selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. Monitoring tracked availability rather than correctness, so the cluster continued to report healthy throughout.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Database errors affecting the billing service. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the time-series store, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Request throughput on the SQLite metadata store rose steadily over 9 hours and the webhook dispatcher began shedding requests, with no change in traffic volume.
root_cause: A query plan on the invoices table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Reduced availability in ca-central.
root_cause: A node in ca-central entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone.

issue: The majority of legitimate requests to the CLI were dropped during a sustained attack.
root_cause: An attack targeted an endpoint on the audit log writer whose responses were expensive to generate and not cached, so a modest request rate was enough to exhaust backend capacity.
solution: Added caching and a strict rate limit to the expensive endpoint, and placed it behind authentication so it cannot be reached anonymously at volume.

issue: Read and write errors against the Kafka topic. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the ledger table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the leader elector rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the leader elector to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to a single production cell because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the catalogue API started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the catalogue API within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The entitlement service slowed progressively over 1 hour 12 minutes, with garbage-collection pause time degrading while CPU and memory stayed within normal bounds.
root_cause: A cache in front of the MySQL replica set was configured with an expiry short enough that most reads missed.
solution: Lengthened the cache expiry to a value matched to how often the underlying data actually changes, which raised the hit rate and returned latency to normal.

issue: Database errors affecting the geocoding service.
root_cause: The connection pool for the geocoding service was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the Kafka topic would accept and new connections were refused.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: The geocoding service unavailable due to a database fault. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An index on the devices table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the DynamoDB table. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal.

issue: The messaging bridge was removed from rotation in us-east despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 78%.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the messaging bridge responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the serialisation layer expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 51 minutes, while the payments themselves completed normally.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the queue consumer made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered. Failed attempts were retried by customers, which produced further load on an already-constrained path.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the queue consumer to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to the production fleet. Impact was limited to the Sydney region.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the pricing engine started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the pricing engine within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Lower-priority processing in the primary region was delayed by 1 hour 12 minutes during planned maintenance.
root_cause: Capacity removed for maintenance was not replaced before the upgrade began, so the two activities overlapped and the remaining headroom was consumed by higher-priority work. Remaining capacity absorbed the redirected load until it too was saturated, which widened the impact.
solution: Paused the upgrade until repair work finished and added a capacity check that must pass before a rolling upgrade starts.

issue: Errors on the reporting UI following a recent change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the sync service did not set, so the cache layer silently rejected every new instance. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the cache layer to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: The notification service degraded sharply with no deploy to explain it, and p99 latency on the ClickHouse cluster rose steadily for 38 minutes. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A new query against the subscriptions table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the ClickHouse cluster. The query planner had no recent statistics for the affected relation, so it continued choosing a plan that no longer suited the data.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: A routine library upgrade left the recommendation service unable to serve traffic in production.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The sidecar proxy had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the sidecar proxy to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: The geocoding service was unavailable for 38 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A maintenance procedure intended to clear a lagging replica was executed against the primary node of the MySQL replica set. Snapshot jobs had been failing silently for weeks, so the newest usable backup was considerably older than the retention policy implied.
solution: Restored from the newest usable snapshot, accepting the resulting data loss, then required a second engineer to confirm any destructive database operation and added alerting on backup success rather than only on failure.

issue: Callers of the audit log writer saw response times multiply for 1 hour 47 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The config loader began synchronously calling the upstream CDN on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to the upstream CDN back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: API tokens for the recommendation service were rejected as invalid for 1 hour 47 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the retry handler was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation. Because the failure was in the credential path rather than the application, every feature behind sign-in became unreachable.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover.

issue: Scheduled disbursements in the billing service did not execute on their intended date.
root_cause: A validation rule added to the cache layer rejected recipient records missing a newly-required field.
solution: Backfilled the missing field, released the held payouts, and changed the cache layer to surface a rejected record as an alert instead of an indefinite queue. A deadline was introduced so a payment attempt fails fast instead of consuming capacity it cannot use.

issue: 42% of requests to the recommendation service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning errors for a subset of requests. The health checker retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the upstream CDN.

issue: The search API availability fell by 3% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the Cassandra ring.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Processing in the sync service did not complete as expected.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The token validator had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Added response validation in the token validator so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The search API degraded in eu-west for 38 minutes and automated failover did not fully restore capacity.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the search API, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down.

issue: Latency on the web dashboard crept upward across the day with no corresponding rise in traffic.
root_cause: A cache key for the export worker included a request-unique value, so entries were never reused and every call was effectively a cold read against the MySQL replica set.
solution: Removed the request-unique component from the cache key so entries are shared across equivalent requests, and added a hit-rate metric with alerting.

issue: The document indexer shedding requests under load.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the document indexer had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the document indexer rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Data access failures in production.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the Redis cache tier. The affected replicas entered recovery, which pushed their load onto the remainder and cascaded into a broader capacity shortfall. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock.

issue: Background jobs in the asset pipeline stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of eight thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the sessions table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the admission controller rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.

root_cause: A node in the Frankfurt region entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.

issue: Sign-in and authorisation errors on the webhooks endpoint.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the token validator was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.

issue: The media transcoder failed to start in the primary region after a dependency upgrade, and the majority of requests to the public API returned errors.

solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps. issue: Calls to the asset pipeline were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 94% of clients.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the sidecar proxy identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the sidecar proxy so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: Requests to the geocoding service failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.

Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.

solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.
