solution: Suspended affected integrations immediately, then coordinated with each provider to revoke and reissue every token and key that had been held, rotating internal credentials before resuming service.

issue: Sign-in and authorisation errors on the reporting UI.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the MongoDB shard past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions.

issue: Requests to the checkout service failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the checkout service started with settings it could not validate. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the checkout service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the billing service did not restore service and left the time-series store in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the time-series store in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the billing service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Internal name resolution failed across the primary cluster and services could no longer reach one another for 1 hour 12 minutes.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting the primary cluster.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production.

issue: The catalogue API degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the catalogue API stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the catalogue API actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Processing in the search API did not complete as expected.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the search API was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: 78% of requests to the admin console were served by an unintended backend for 23 minutes.
root_cause: An edge configuration set the backend target inside a request handler, but a later step in the same configuration restarted request processing, which reset the target to the first entry in the list rather than the intended one.
solution: Corrected the configuration so the backend target survives the restart step, and added a test that asserts backend selection after a mid-request restart.

issue: Just under half of requests to the media transcoder were rejected at the edge while the service itself reported healthy.
root_cause: A filtering rule was changed directly on the edge tier outside the normal pipeline, so the change did not appear in deployment history. Responders spent most of the incident examining recent releases before drift detection surfaced the untracked edit. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band edge change and restricted write access so edits outside the pipeline are blocked, with drift detection alerting on any that still occur.

issue: Processing in the catalogue API did not complete as expected.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the MySQL replica set was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: 31% of requests to the partner API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced a regional fault. The recommendation service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: The billing service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the billing service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the billing service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: A low-risk change to the production fleet resulted in a wider outage than its scope suggested.
root_cause: The change was tested against a single node but applied to the fleet simultaneously, so a defect that one node could absorb removed capacity everywhere at once.
solution: Reverted the change and introduced staged application across the fleet with a health gate between stages.

issue: The search API could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in ap-northeast.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the search API was raised past what any node in ap-northeast could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region.

issue: Capacity in us-west fell by 63% and the identity service began shedding requests.
root_cause: A failing component presented inconsistent state to different members of the cluster behind the identity service, so health checks disagreed about which nodes were usable and repeated leadership changes left the cluster read-only.
solution: Removed the partially-failed component from service so a stable leader could be elected, then reviewed how the cluster handles conflicting information from a component that is neither fully up nor fully down. Capacity headroom was increased so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the inventory service, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the inventory service failed to reconnect after a restart of the retry handler and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. Routing configuration now scales with the fleet rather than being maintained as a fixed value.

issue: Writes to the webhooks table began failing with a constraint error, blocking new records in the media transcoder for 38 minutes.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the webhooks table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected. Because the failure mode was a slowdown rather than an error, retries added further load to an already-saturated cluster.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The ingest gateway was unavailable for 38 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the MySQL replica set.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Reports generated by the billing service contained figures that did not reconcile with the underlying records.
root_cause: A rounding change in the sidecar proxy was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports.

issue: Security incident affecting the notification service.
root_cause: A distributed attack saturated the edge capacity serving the SDK. Mitigation rules existed but were scoped to a traffic profile the attack did not match, so they did not engage automatically. Existing mitigation rules were scoped to a different traffic profile, so they did not engage automatically.
solution: Applied mitigation manually to absorb the attack, then broadened the automatic rules to cover this traffic profile and raised edge capacity headroom.

issue: The partner API displayed incorrect values to 18% of users for most of the working day while every service reported healthy.
root_cause: A rounding change in the token validator was applied at an intermediate step rather than at presentation, so each subsequent calculation compounded the difference and totals drifted from the source records. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Moved rounding to the presentation layer so intermediate calculations retain full precision, and recomputed the affected reports. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Access to the reporting UI denied for a subset of users.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the rate limiter uses to validate credentials for the document indexer.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect.

issue: Background jobs in the recommendation service stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of a dozen thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the batch consumer rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the batch consumer to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: The sync service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in us-east. The sync service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Callers of the identity service saw response times multiply for 3 hours 20 minutes under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the identity service.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Per-tenant concurrency limits were introduced so one caller cannot consume a shared pool.

issue: New deployments of the inventory service hung in a pending state for 23 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the inventory service did not set, so the connection pool silently rejected every new instance. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the connection pool to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the checkout service made the incident worse and extended impact by most of the working day.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the time-series store, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the time-series store, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: Queries against the devices table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the chat backend began timing out for 78% of requests. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A new query against the devices table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the MongoDB shard. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the billing service.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the billing service expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: Processing in the ingest gateway did not complete as expected. Both the reporting UI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A third-party email provider experienced a regional fault. The ingest gateway depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party email provider recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: A maintenance window on the production fleet that was expected to be routine caused 14 minutes of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The change was tested against a single node but applied to the fleet simultaneously, so a defect that one node could absorb removed capacity everywhere at once. The dependency had no degraded mode, so an upstream fault removed the feature rather than reducing it.
solution: Reverted the change and introduced staged application across the fleet with a health gate between stages.

issue: Requests to the billing service failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the billing service. The new default disagreed with the health checker, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the health checker cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: The webhook dispatcher became unavailable in ap-southeast following a disk failure on a node that continued reporting itself healthy.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the webhook dispatcher failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: A scheduled job in the asset pipeline did not run for 51 minutes and the omission was noticed only when downstream data went stale.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the asset pipeline was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: A traffic spike on the embedded widget pushed the feed builder past its capacity and just under half of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the feed builder had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the feed builder rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the identity service, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the identity service failed to reconnect after a restart of the request router and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data. Every service that resolved the affected name failed together, which made the blast radius far larger than the change implied.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in eu-west.
root_cause: The reporting UI began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. Because each request was individually fast, backend dashboards stayed within normal bounds while callers saw seconds of delay.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time.

issue: The ingest gateway degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the object store bucket.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The sync service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the entitlements table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the shard mapper rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The query planner had no recent statistics for the affected relation, so it continued choosing a plan that no longer suited the data.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the shard mapper to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Read and write errors against the ClickHouse cluster.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the ClickHouse cluster, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: Requests to the document indexer failed across all regions immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the document indexer. The new default disagreed with the config loader, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the config loader cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the checkout service.
root_cause: Session records in the Redis cache tier were keyed differently after a deploy, so existing sessions could not be found and every request fell through to a full re-authentication against the serialisation layer. The error surfaced to users as an invalid credential, so support initially treated it as a user-side problem.
solution: Restored the previous key format and added a dual-read path so a key change can no longer invalidate every existing session at once.

issue: The billing service exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected a small subset of requests.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the maximum payload size well below the load it had previously handled.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion.

issue: A subset of transactions in the chat backend were recorded twice over a 9 hours window.
root_cause: A retry in the admission controller re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to a partner inventory feed so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the partner API.
root_cause: A signing key used by the token validator was rotated without updating every validator, so tokens issued after the rotation were rejected by the services still holding the previous key.
solution: Distributed the new key to all validators and changed rotation to publish the new key and accept both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: The partner API began returning errors for 11% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the geocoding service itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the primary cluster because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the geocoding service started with settings it could not validate. The affected path is exercised only under production traffic, so pre-production checks had reported success.

issue: Routing for the scheduling service sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting just under half of traffic.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the scheduling service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend. The failure removed the paths engineers would normally use to diagnose it, which extended time to recovery considerably.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the session store to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Calls to the recommendation service were rate-limited far more often than usual after a maintenance window, affecting 24% of clients.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the health checker identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the health checker so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The catalogue API unable to reach its dependencies.
root_cause: A certificate chain was deployed without its intermediate, so clients with a strict trust store rejected the connection while clients that cached the intermediate succeeded.
solution: Redeployed the full chain including the intermediate and added a verification step that validates the served chain against a strict trust store after each deploy.

issue: The notification service was degraded for 51 minutes because of a fault at the upstream CDN rather than in the organisation's own systems. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: The upstream CDN began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The rate limiter had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the rate limiter so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the SDK. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the cache layer caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the cache layer, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: Healthy instances of the audit log writer were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 38 minutes window.

The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the queue consumer expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Batch workloads on the webhook dispatcher ran at reduced throughput for 2 hours 5 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected.

solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region. solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a partner inventory feed.

issue: Traffic to the entitlement service failing to reach its destination.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the entitlement service expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Retries did not help because the resolution step failed before any connection was attempted.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently.

issue: Federated login to the export worker broke for a subset of tenants while local accounts worked normally.
root_cause: A stricter assertion-validation rule was enabled in the rate limiter. Identity providers that sent an optional attribute in a non-canonical form had previously been accepted and were now rejected, so their tenants could not complete sign-in. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Relaxed the rule to accept both forms of the attribute while affected providers were contacted, then staged future validation changes behind a per-tenant warning period. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: 78% of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting production. The defect was not caught in pre-production because the test environment resolved names through a different path, so it first appeared in production. Negative results were cached downstream, so the failure persisted for some clients after the underlying record was corrected.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production.

issue: Leadership for the audit log writer changed repeatedly over 9 hours, and some work was executed twice. Both the SDK and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: Health checks in us-east disagreed about which instances were reachable, so repeated elections occurred and each new leader began work the previous one had not finished.
solution: Stabilised the health checks and required a quorum before an election proceeds, then made the work idempotent so a repeated execution is harmless.

issue: Roughly a third of API clients received throttling responses from the entitlement service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the config loader identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. As queues grew, client retries added load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the config loader so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The majority of users could not sign in to the public API for 6 hours 10 minutes, with no clear pattern by region or account type. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the config loader uses to validate credentials for the recommendation service. Sessions established before the change continued to work, which made the impact look smaller than it was.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The scheduling service unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to all regions because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the scheduling service started with settings it could not validate. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the scheduling service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: A handful of merchants did not receive delivery callbacks from the sync service and were unaware of completed transactions.
root_cause: A serialisation change in the token validator made some callback payloads unencodable. The failures were counted as successful dequeues, so the backlog drained without anything being delivered.
solution: Fixed the serialisation path, replayed the affected callbacks, and changed the token validator to treat an encoding failure as a delivery failure that retries. Idempotency keys are now required on every call to the processor so a retry cannot create a second payment.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the recommendation service.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the connection pool identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. As queues grew, client retries added load to the same saturated path and amplified the delay well beyond the original shortfall.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the connection pool so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The identity service was degraded for 2 hours 5 minutes because of an outage at the cloud provider block-storage service.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The identity service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Served a degraded response while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Latency on the webhook dispatcher was 42% higher in one region for most of the working day with no configuration difference.
root_cause: Instances of the webhook dispatcher in eu-central were routed to the Elasticsearch index in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Repointed the webhook dispatcher at the local replica of the Elasticsearch index and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Requests to the recommendation service failed across production immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. Both the embedded widget and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the recommendation service.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the retry handler cannot parse before it reaches production. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Capacity in the primary region fell by 78% and the entitlement service began shedding requests.
root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in the primary region below what was needed to serve normal traffic. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the shortfall.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: Connectivity failures affecting the notification service.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the notification service expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently.

issue: 11% of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting the shared staging-to-production path.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: The ingest gateway became slow in us-west only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in us-west left the ingest gateway running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic.
solution: Restored the instance count in us-west and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: Reads from the messaging bridge returned stale data for 51 minutes while writes continued to succeed normally.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Redis cache tier, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: The entitlement service failed to start in sa-east after a dependency upgrade, and 11% of requests to the CLI returned errors. Both the CLI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the health checker still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in a single production cell. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps.

issue: The media transcoder degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the media transcoder. The new default disagreed with the shard mapper, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the shard mapper cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: Service disruption traced to a configuration change.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the reporting API, and the rule applied to the primary cluster rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: A small subset of service-to-service calls failed with resolution errors after an infrastructure change. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the notification service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. A management path independent of the production routing plane was provisioned so diagnosis no longer depends on the failing component.

issue: The billing service was offline for 4 hours 36 minutes after a power event at the facility hosting all regions. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting all regions was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed. Key details of the provider's failover arrangement had not been documented in advance, which slowed diagnosis.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: Single sign-on to the public API failed for 31% of enterprise tenants for 23 minutes.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the retry handler caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the retry handler, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: Errors on the partner API following a recent change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the pricing engine did not set, so the job scheduler silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the job scheduler to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Authentication requests to the scheduling service timed out for 11% of attempts after a scheduled change. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the object store bucket past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: Background jobs in the asset pipeline stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of six thousand items accumulated.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the connection pool rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the connection pool to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Payment confirmations stopped reaching merchants for 14 minutes, while the payments themselves completed normally. Both the SDK and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A change to the queue infrastructure behind the audit log writer caused a subset of delivery workers to lose their connection without raising an error.
solution: Replayed the undelivered callbacks once identified, then added active health checks on delivery workers rather than inferring health from an absence of errors.

issue: Background jobs in the messaging bridge stopped being picked up after a deploy, and a backlog of two thousand items accumulated. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the audit table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the config loader rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Lock waits propagated to unrelated statements, so the impact spread well beyond the queries that caused it.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the config loader to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: New deployments of the billing service hung in a pending state for 4 hours 36 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: A resource request in the deployment manifest for the billing service was raised past what any node in ap-northeast could satisfy, so the scheduler had nowhere to place new instances and left them pending indefinitely. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Lowered the resource request back to a schedulable value and added a check that fails the pipeline when a request exceeds the largest available node in the target region. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Authentication requests to the feed builder timed out for a handful of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the time-series store past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the document indexer. Impact was limited to eu-west.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the document indexer for every caller. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth.

issue: The identity service was removed from rotation in the Frankfurt region despite being healthy, dropping capacity by 11%.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time.

issue: Data access failures in the production fleet.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the DynamoDB table.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: 24% of users on the reporting UI saw an unreleased interface for 6 hours 10 minutes before it was withdrawn.
root_cause: A feature flag for the document indexer was created with a default-on value rather than default-off.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: The billing service degraded after a routine rollout. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the billing service stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the billing service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: The geocoding service timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: The health checker began synchronously calling the managed Kubernetes control plane on a path that had previously been asynchronous.
solution: Moved the call to the managed Kubernetes control plane back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency. Load shedding was added so the service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline.

issue: Requests to the feed builder queued and timed out while the ClickHouse cluster itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: The connection pool for the feed builder was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the ClickHouse cluster would accept and new connections were refused.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The pricing engine stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 14 minutes.
root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the documents table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the health checker rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the health checker to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the metrics agent identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the metrics agent so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: The chat backend became slow in sa-east only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: Instances of the chat backend in sa-east were routed to the MongoDB shard in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the chat backend at the local replica of the MongoDB shard and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: The sync service stopped processing queued work silently; no errors were logged for 51 minutes.
root_cause: A migration renamed a column the job scheduler selects on. The query returned an empty result rather than failing, so the dispatcher concluded there was no work to do. The query planner had no recent statistics for the affected relation, so it continued choosing a plan that no longer suited the data.
solution: Restored the expected column name, replayed the backlog, and added an alert on a dispatcher reporting zero available work while the queue is non-empty.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the media transcoder in ap-northeast.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting the production fleet was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The public API began returning errors for the majority of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the document indexer itself. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the shared staging-to-production path because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the document indexer started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the document indexer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Database errors affecting the export worker.
root_cause: A uniqueness constraint added to the events table during a migration did not account for historical rows that legitimately shared a value, so inserts touching those keys were rejected.
solution: Dropped the constraint, de-duplicated the historical rows, and re-applied it as a partial constraint scoped to records created after the cutover.

issue: Nodes running the entitlement service restarted repeatedly on out-of-memory conditions, and cluster leadership moved between them.
root_cause: A background agent on each node retried a failing call to a partner inventory feed in a loop, retaining the context of every attempt.
solution: Bounded the retry loop and released the context between attempts, then added alerting specific to this agent's memory use since the node's normal dynamic usage had masked the growth.

issue: 31% of requests to the export worker failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced an outage in us-east. The export worker called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Health checks tested process liveness rather than the ability to do useful work, so the fault stayed hidden.
solution: Served a degraded response while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: 78% of requests to the public API failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A third-party email provider experienced a regional fault. The reporting API depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party email provider recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The billing service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in ca-central. The billing service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

issue: Database errors affecting the media transcoder.
root_cause: A new query against the sessions table shipped without a supporting index. Volume was low enough in testing to hide the cost, but at production volume each call scanned the whole table and exhausted the read capacity of the Kafka topic. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Added the supporting index and introduced a review step that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: The export worker ran with configuration from the previous release for 1 hour 47 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the export worker stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the export worker actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: Batch workloads on the audit log writer ran at reduced throughput for 6 hours 10 minutes while interactive traffic was unaffected.
root_cause: Planned repair work coincided with a rolling software upgrade across the fleet in the primary region, reducing capacity available to lower-priority traffic classes.
solution: Allowed both activities to complete, after which capacity for lower-priority classes returned to normal, and added a scheduling rule preventing maintenance and fleet upgrades from overlapping in one region. A circuit breaker and cached fallback were added so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Requests to the export worker queued and timed out while the Kafka topic itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion.

issue: 55% of requests to the checkout service failed due to a fault outside the organisation's own infrastructure.
root_cause: A partner inventory feed experienced an outage in ap-northeast. The checkout service called it synchronously with no fallback, so the upstream failure became a full failure of the dependent feature rather than a degraded one. The redundancy that was expected to cover this failure shared an upstream component with the path that failed.
solution: Served a degraded response while a partner inventory feed recovered, then added a circuit breaker and a cached fallback so an upstream outage reduces functionality instead of removing it.

root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the pricing engine and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock.

issue: The mobile apps began returning errors for 63% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the messaging bridge itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the messaging bridge. The new default disagreed with the session store, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the session store cannot parse before it reaches production.

issue: The SDK began returning errors for 78% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the checkout service itself.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the checkout service. The new default disagreed with the job scheduler, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the job scheduler cannot parse before it reaches all regions.

issue: The recommendation service affected by an infrastructure event.
root_cause: An external geolocation API began returning errors for a subset of requests. The shard mapper retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to an external geolocation API.

issue: 55% of requests to the reporting UI failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: An external geolocation API began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The queue consumer had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Added response validation in the queue consumer so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

root_cause: A deploy changed the stored type of a field in the sessions table. Rows written before and after the change had different types, and the strict validation in the rate limiter rejected every row it scanned, so it stopped claiming work without reporting an error. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Shipped a build that tolerated both field types, drained the backlog with temporary additional capacity, and changed the rate limiter to treat an unreadable row as an error rather than a skip.

issue: Payouts from the asset pipeline were delayed by most of the working day for 85% of recipients.
root_cause: A timezone change in the scheduling configuration for the asset pipeline moved the payout cutoff past the window during which an upstream payment processor accepts same-day instructions, so batches were held until the next cycle.
solution: Restored the scheduling configuration to the correct timezone and pinned the cutoff to the processor's stated window rather than a local time.

issue: Payment records inconsistent for a subset of customers.
root_cause: A synchronous call from the recommendation service to the managed DNS provider became the bottleneck under peak load. With no concurrency limit, queued payment attempts consumed worker capacity and timed out before reaching the processor. Merchants had no way to distinguish a delayed payment from a failed one, which generated substantial support load.
solution: Added a concurrency limit and queue with a deadline so payment attempts fail fast rather than consuming capacity, and provisioned headroom sized against peak forecasts. Idempotency keys are now required on every call to the processor so a retry cannot create a second payment.

issue: The scheduling service unable to reach its dependencies. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the scheduling service were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: Elevated memory use in the asset pipeline in ap-northeast.
root_cause: Memory was lost to fragmentation rather than a genuine leak. An aligned-allocation pattern in the queue consumer interacted poorly with the system allocator in that environment, permanently fragmenting the pool even though every allocation was correctly freed. Because only one environment was affected, the problem was initially attributed to that environment rather than the code.
solution: Replaced the aligned-allocation pattern with a dedicated allocator that avoids the fragmenting path, which stopped the steady growth under sustained load.

issue: The export worker silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the webhooks table without updates.
root_cause: A clock change moved the job's window into a period when the Kafka topic was unavailable for maintenance, and the job treated the failure as a completed run rather than retrying.
solution: Moved the job outside the maintenance window and changed it to retry on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: The identity service was degraded for most of the working day because of a fault at the managed DNS provider rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The rate limiter had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Added response validation in the rate limiter so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.
