root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the inventory service. The new default disagreed with the metrics agent, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the metrics agent cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: Internal name resolution failed across all regions and services could no longer reach one another for 9 hours. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the search API and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty. Everything that depended on that name began failing resolution. Every service that resolved the affected name failed together, which made the blast radius far larger than the change implied.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in eu-central.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the catalogue API.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client.

issue: The geocoding service exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected just under half of requests.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the file-descriptor limit well below the load it had previously handled.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the identity service made the incident worse and extended impact by 23 minutes.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the primary Postgres cluster in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the identity service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Elevated response times on the CLI.
root_cause: Instances of the webhook dispatcher in the Sydney region were routed to the Cassandra ring in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost.
solution: Repointed the webhook dispatcher at the local replica of the Cassandra ring and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: Incorrect behaviour observed on the admin console.
root_cause: The managed DNS provider experienced a regional fault. The messaging bridge depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. The affected process ran infrequently, so the next scheduled run was the earliest point recovery could be verified.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the managed DNS provider recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Network errors between services in a single production cell.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the billing service failed to reconnect after a restart of the connection pool and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data. Clients held the stale answer for the full lifetime of their cache, so recovery was staggered rather than immediate.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age.

issue: Read and write errors against the object store bucket.
root_cause: A schema migration on the accounts table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the export worker.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the queue consumer identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the queue consumer so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports.

issue: Requests to the ingest gateway queued and timed out while the object store bucket itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the connection limit well below the load it had previously handled.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: The sync service could not scale out during a traffic increase even though spare capacity was available in eu-west.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the sync service did not set, so the leader elector silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the leader elector to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: The catalogue API degraded after a routine rollout.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the MongoDB shard, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the MongoDB shard, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: The media transcoder was degraded for 14 minutes because of a fault at the cloud provider block-storage service rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service experienced a regional fault. The media transcoder depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available.
solution: Served a reduced experience while the cloud provider block-storage service recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

issue: The identity service was offline for 6 hours 10 minutes after a power event at the facility hosting a single production cell.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the identity service were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: The feed builder shedding requests under load.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the job scheduler treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing. Load shedding was added so the service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline.

issue: Increased latency and timeouts in eu-central.
root_cause: Instances of the reporting API in eu-central were routed to the time-series store in a different region after a failover, so every query crossed a regional boundary and paid the round-trip cost. Latency rose gradually rather than stepping, so threshold-based alerting did not fire until impact was already broad.
solution: Repointed the reporting API at the local replica of the time-series store and added an alert when a service's data path crosses a region boundary unexpectedly.

issue: A maintenance window on the shared staging-to-production path that was expected to be routine caused most of the working day of unplanned downtime.
root_cause: The procedure assumed the network equipment serving the shared staging-to-production path was configured to handle a traffic pattern it had never actually been verified against. The resulting flood affected the whole environment rather than the isolated segment that was intended. Because the change was outside the normal release path, it did not appear in any deployment history.
solution: Reconfigured the equipment to handle the traffic pattern correctly and added a pre-maintenance verification step covering it explicitly. A reconciliation check against source records was added so a discrepancy is surfaced automatically.

issue: Read and write errors against the primary Postgres cluster. Both the CLI and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the per-tenant quota well below the load it had previously handled.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the search API in a single production cell.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the search API stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the search API actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: 85% of users on the web dashboard saw an unreleased interface for 1 hour 47 minutes before it was withdrawn.
root_cause: A targeting rule meant to match a single internal tenant used a prefix comparison, so it matched a large set of production tenant identifiers that shared the same prefix. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Corrected the targeting rule to an exact-match comparison and added a dry-run report that lists which tenants a rule will match before it is saved.

issue: Users reported the recommendation service being unresponsive although every backend dashboard looked healthy.
root_cause: A client-side change in the admin console issued one request per item rather than a single batched call.
solution: Restored the batched call so a page issues one request instead of many, and added a client-side latency metric so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal. Autoscaling was re-keyed on queue depth so capacity is added while requests are waiting rather than computing.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the chat backend in sa-east.
root_cause: The cloud provider block-storage service began returning errors for a subset of requests. The rate limiter retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency. Higher-priority traffic was protected as designed, which meant sustained degradation for everything below it.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to the cloud provider block-storage service.

issue: 78% of programmatic clients lost access to the reporting UI without any credential change on their side.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the object store bucket did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the connection pool could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the object store bucket and changed the connection pool to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster.

issue: The catalogue API became slow in sa-east only, while the same service performed normally elsewhere.
root_cause: A capacity reduction in sa-east left the catalogue API running on fewer instances than its load required, and the regional router continued sending a full share of traffic. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Restored the instance count in sa-east and changed the router to weight traffic by healthy capacity rather than by a fixed regional share.

issue: The export worker silently skipped its periodic processing, leaving the documents table without updates.
root_cause: The scheduler entry for the export worker was removed as part of an unrelated cleanup. Nothing monitored for a job that fails to start, so the absence produced no signal at all. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Restored the scheduler entry, backfilled the missed processing, and added dead-man alerting that fires when an expected run does not occur. The change path was brought inside the normal release process so it appears in deployment history.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the webhook dispatcher, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the webhook dispatcher failed to reconnect after a restart of the admission controller and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age.

issue: The checkout service ran with configuration from the previous release for 14 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the token validator but the checkout service reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: A power interruption took the shared staging-to-production path offline and recovery took considerably longer than planned.
root_cause: A utility power interruption at the facility hosting the shared staging-to-production path was expected to be covered by backup generation, which did not engage as designed.
solution: Worked with the facility provider to restore power and bring systems back, then obtained full documentation of the failover design and agreed explicit communication commitments for future events.

issue: Data access failures in the production fleet.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the Cassandra ring. Nothing required a second approval for a destructive operation, so it ran unchecked.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: A traffic spike on the SDK pushed the inventory service past its capacity and a handful of requests failed.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the inventory service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the inventory service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: Degraded performance affecting the inventory service.
root_cause: A traffic increase coincided with a reduced number of available workers in the inventory service.
solution: Restored worker capacity and separated retry traffic from first-attempt requests so a retry storm can no longer crowd out new work, then added backoff with jitter on the client. Load shedding was added so the service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline.

issue: The production fleet lost external connectivity for 1 hour 12 minutes, including the remote access paths needed to diagnose the problem. Impact was limited to us-west.
root_cause: An automated policy update removed prefix filters from the route export configuration, so the edge advertised internal ranges externally and traffic for the scheduling service was drawn away from its intended path.
solution: Reinstated the prefix filters and added a validation step that blocks a route export policy which would advertise internal ranges. A rule was adopted that resolution-dependent tooling may not be used to repair a resolution outage.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the partner API was blocked for 9 hours with no recent deploy to explain it. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the sync service, and the rule applied to all regions rather than a single tenant. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop.

issue: New deployments of the recommendation service hung in a pending state for 14 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the recommendation service did not set, so the admission controller silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the admission controller to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: Requests to the feed builder failed across the production fleet immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the feed builder started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the feed builder within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Just under half of requests to the SDK failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The metrics agent had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the metrics agent so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: Memory growth in the ingest gateway leading to restarts.
root_cause: The request router registered a listener for each request but never removed it, so the registry grew for the lifetime of the process.
solution: Removed the listener when a request completes and added a bound on the registry size, after which memory stabilised under sustained load.

issue: Requests to the web dashboard failed TLS negotiation for 24% of clients starting at a fixed time of day.
root_cause: The certificate presented by the edge tier for the identity service expired. Renewal was automated but the automation had been failing quietly for several weeks because its credential had been rotated without updating the job.
solution: Issued and deployed a replacement certificate, repaired the renewal job's credential, and added alerting on certificate expiry that pages well before the deadline rather than reporting silently.

issue: The inventory service exhausted its database connections during a traffic increase and rejected just under half of requests.
root_cause: A code change moved connection acquisition outside the request scope, so connections were held for the lifetime of a worker instead of a single query. The pool reached the thread-pool bound well below the load it had previously handled. Connections accumulated faster than they were released, so callers queued behind a pool that never recovered on its own.
solution: Returned connection acquisition to request scope so connections are released promptly, and added a pool-saturation metric with alerting before exhaustion.

issue: The notification service availability fell by 11% during the last stage of a long-running schema change.
root_cause: The concluding step rewrote the webhooks table in place rather than swapping a prepared copy, so every replica applied the rewrite simultaneously and fell out of the read pool together.
solution: Brought replicas back in a staggered sequence and reworked the migration to apply the final step to one replica at a time. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Memory growth in the scheduling service leading to restarts. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A background agent on each node retried a failing call to a third-party SMS gateway in a loop, retaining the context of every attempt.
solution: Bounded the retry loop and released the context between attempts, then added alerting specific to this agent's memory use since the node's normal dynamic usage had masked the growth. The cache was given a size limit and an eviction policy so it cannot grow with the number of distinct keys.

issue: 42% of API clients received throttling responses from the notification service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the job scheduler identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Upstream callers had no timeout of their own, so the slowdown propagated into services that were otherwise healthy.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the job scheduler so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Retries now use exponential backoff with jitter, and a concurrency cap bounds in-flight calls to the dependency.

issue: Queue depth on the object store bucket rose steadily over 6 hours 10 minutes and the pricing engine began shedding requests, with no change in traffic volume.
root_cause: A query plan on the sessions table flipped from an index scan to a sequential scan once the table crossed a size threshold, and the planner had no statistics recent enough to choose correctly. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Refreshed planner statistics and added a hint pinning the intended index, with a scheduled statistics job to prevent the plan from flipping again. Replication lag is now an alerted metric rather than being inferred from replica availability.

issue: The feed builder was unavailable for 1 hour 47 minutes and some records written shortly before the incident could not be recovered. Impact was limited to eu-central.
root_cause: A cleanup task matched on a hostname pattern that also matched the primary node of the MongoDB shard.
solution: Rebuilt the primary from a replica, added an explicit allow-list for destructive automation, and introduced regular restore drills to verify snapshots are usable. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: Errors on the SDK following a recent change.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The sidecar proxy had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the sidecar proxy to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the notification service in the primary cluster. Both the web dashboard and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the notification service stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the notification service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: Authentication requests to the feed builder timed out for 3% of attempts after a scheduled change.
root_cause: A caching change caused the session lookup to scan far more data than intended on each miss, driving load on the Elasticsearch index past what it could serve.
solution: Reduced load with a connection throttle, adjusted it in careful increments to avoid overshooting, and rewrote the lookup to read only the missing entries rather than scanning whole partitions. Error responses now distinguish an infrastructure failure from an invalid credential so support can triage correctly.

issue: Single sign-on to the admin console failed for 31% of enterprise tenants for 4 hours 36 minutes.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the connection pool caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the connection pool, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential.

issue: The SDK unreachable for a subset of clients.
root_cause: Two automation components raced to update the same DNS record for the identity service and overwrote each other, ultimately leaving the record empty.
solution: Restored the records manually and disabled the conflicting automation until it was serialised behind a single writer with a lock. A validation step now blocks a change that would withdraw routes or empty a record set in use.

issue: The embedded widget became slow for 42% of users while backend services reported normal queue depth.
root_cause: The embedded widget began requesting an uncached resource on every navigation. Server-side timings remained flat because the cost was in the number of round trips rather than in any single response. Requests consumed worker capacity before timing out, so the service spent its budget on work that was discarded.
solution: Made the resource cacheable with an appropriate expiry and added synthetic monitoring that measures end-to-end page load rather than only server response time.

issue: Reads from the scheduling service returned stale data for 4 hours 36 minutes while writes continued to succeed normally.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Kafka topic, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: 3% of reads served by the checkout service reflected data minutes behind the primary.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the MongoDB shard stalled without raising an error. Monitoring tracked replica availability but not replication lag, so the stall was invisible until customers reported inconsistency.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. A saturation metric with alerting was added so the limit is visible before it is reached.

issue: The ingest gateway failed to start in us-east after a dependency upgrade, and 94% of requests to the public API returned errors.
root_cause: A transitive dependency was upgraded across a minor version that changed a default serialisation setting. The connection pool had relied on the previous default, so it could no longer read payloads written by its own earlier version.
solution: Pinned the dependency to the previous version to restore service, then updated the connection pool to set the serialisation option explicitly rather than relying on a library default.

issue: Routing for the audit log writer sent requests to the wrong backend after an edge configuration change, affecting 7% of traffic.
root_cause: A routing rule matched on a path prefix that overlapped with another service's namespace, so requests intended for the audit log writer were dispatched to a neighbouring backend.
solution: Made the matching rule specific enough to exclude the overlapping namespace and added a conflict check that rejects two rules matching the same path.

issue: Roughly a third of reads served by the entitlement service reflected data minutes behind the primary.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the Elasticsearch index stalled without raising an error.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: Requests to the recommendation service queued and timed out while the ClickHouse cluster itself remained lightly loaded.
root_cause: The connection pool for the recommendation service was sized for a previous instance count.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value.

issue: A configuration change applied cleanly but had no effect on the behaviour of the identity service in a single production cell.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the identity service stopped reading in an earlier refactor. Nothing validated that the path was still consumed, so the apply reported success while changing nothing.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the identity service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it.

issue: Just under half of reads served by the geocoding service reflected data minutes behind the primary. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Cassandra ring, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically.

issue: Just under half of API clients received throttling responses from the geocoding service despite being well under their quota. Impact was limited to sa-east.
root_cause: A rate-limit counter was keyed on a value that reset during the maintenance window, so the session store treated long-standing clients as new and applied the stricter unestablished-client limit.
solution: Re-seeded the counters from the previous values and changed the limiter to fail open for established clients when its key is missing.

issue: API tokens for the asset pipeline were rejected as invalid for 38 minutes even though they had not expired.
root_cause: A change to token hashing in the health checker was deployed without a compatibility path, so previously-issued tokens no longer matched their stored representation.
solution: Added a compatibility path that verifies against both the old and new representations, and scheduled re-hashing as a background migration rather than a cutover. Successful authentication rate is now monitored rather than only endpoint availability.

issue: The recommendation service timing out for a subset of callers.
root_cause: Incoming volume rose sharply and the recommendation service had no admission control, so it accepted more work than it could complete.
solution: Added admission control so the recommendation service rejects work it cannot complete within its deadline instead of accepting and failing it, and provisioned headroom for bursts of this size.

issue: The inventory service was degraded for 2 hours 5 minutes because of a fault at a downstream KYC vendor rather than in the organisation's own systems.
root_cause: A downstream KYC vendor experienced a regional fault. The inventory service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Impact was limited to a subset of users, which delayed detection and complicated reproduction.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a downstream KYC vendor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: Healthy instances of the reporting API were ejected from the load balancer pool over a 4 hours 36 minutes window. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: A configuration change altered how the reporting API responded to health probes. The response was still successful but no longer matched the string the connection pool expected, so every instance was marked unhealthy and pulled from rotation. The rollout had no health gate between stages, so the faulty state reached all instances at once.
solution: Reverted the health-probe change so responses matched again, and decoupled the probe contract from the response body so a formatting change cannot mark a healthy instance down. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the geocoding service did not restore service and left the Kafka topic in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the Kafka topic in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the geocoding service failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. The change passed review because its diff looked small, and its effect at runtime was not obvious from the text.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer. Alerting was changed to correlate symptom onset with recent changes so the trigger is surfaced automatically.

issue: 31% of requests to the web dashboard failed while every internal component reported healthy. Severity varied by tenant depending on request mix.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The health checker had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Added response validation in the health checker so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one. The job now retries on failure rather than recording an unsuccessful attempt as complete.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the checkout service across a single production cell.
root_cause: An outlier-detection threshold was tightened so a single transient error was enough to eject an instance, and no cap limited how much of the fleet could be removed at once. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Restored the previous thresholds and added a ceiling on the share of a fleet that outlier detection may eject at one time.

issue: The asset pipeline stopped processing requests for 6 hours 10 minutes with no error logged and no rise in load. Both the mobile apps and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: Two code paths in the health checker acquired the same pair of locks in opposite orders. Under a particular interleaving each held one lock and waited for the other, so the workers stopped making progress without crashing or logging an error. Recovery required restarting the affected processes, since nothing detected a worker that had stopped making progress.
solution: Restarted the affected workers to clear the deadlock, then imposed a single global lock-ordering rule in the health checker and added a watchdog that restarts a worker making no progress. Fencing tokens were introduced so writes from a superseded leader are rejected.

issue: Legitimate traffic to the web dashboard was blocked for 3 hours 20 minutes with no recent deploy to explain it.
root_cause: A protective rule intended to block a single abusive client was written with a pattern broad enough to match normal traffic to the asset pipeline, and the rule applied to all regions rather than a single tenant.
solution: Narrowed the rule to the intended client, scoped it to a single tenant, and added a staged rollout for edge filtering changes with an automatic revert on a traffic drop. A documented rollback procedure was added for this class of change and tested in a drill.

issue: Reports generated by the export worker contained figures that did not reconcile with the underlying records.
root_cause: A time-zone assumption in the export worker placed events in the wrong reporting period for users outside the primary region, so daily totals were attributed to the adjacent day. The incorrect values were written downstream before the fault was found, so correcting it required a backfill.
solution: Normalised event timestamps to a single zone before aggregation, regenerated the affected periods, and added a reconciliation check against source records. Response validation was added at the boundary so a malformed upstream reply is rejected rather than propagated.

issue: 31% of API clients received throttling responses from the checkout service despite being well under their quota.
root_cause: Maintenance on the token service changed how the health checker identified a caller. Requests that previously counted against a per-tenant quota began counting against a single shared bucket, so unrelated clients exhausted each other's allowance. Load shedding was not configured, so the service accepted more work than it could complete within its deadline.
solution: Restored per-tenant identification in the health checker so quotas are counted separately again, and added an alert on a sudden rise in throttling rate rather than relying on customer reports. Client-side latency is now measured so user-visible slowness is visible even when backend timings look normal.

issue: Service discovery data stopped reaching the notification service, which continued operating on information that grew progressively more stale.
root_cause: The discovery agent on the notification service failed to reconnect after a restart of the cache layer and kept serving its last known snapshot rather than reporting that it had no fresh data.
solution: Fixed the reconnect path and changed the agent to report an error and fail closed when its snapshot exceeds a maximum age. Negative-response cache lifetimes were shortened so a corrected record propagates promptly.

issue: New deployments of the reporting API hung in a pending state for 3 hours 20 minutes, and no new instances joined the pool.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the reporting API did not set, so the sidecar proxy silently rejected every new instance. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the sidecar proxy to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Callers of the entitlement service saw response times multiply for 9 hours under ordinary traffic.
root_cause: The connection pool began synchronously calling the cloud provider block-storage service on a path that had previously been asynchronous. Each request inherited the dependency latency, and the thread pool filled with waiting work.
solution: Moved the call to the cloud provider block-storage service back off the request path, added a timeout and circuit breaker around it, and sized the thread pool against measured dependency latency.

issue: Six hundred payments were double-counted in the sessions table before the discrepancy was detected.
root_cause: A retry in the metrics agent re-sent a payment authorisation that had in fact succeeded but whose response was lost.
solution: Reconciled and reversed the duplicate transactions, then required an idempotency key on every call to the cloud provider block-storage service so a retry can no longer create a second payment.

issue: Users unable to sign in to the reporting UI.
root_cause: A migration of the token store to the time-series store did not carry across tokens issued before a certain date, so the request router could not find them and treated them as invalid rather than reporting a lookup failure. The change had been reviewed as a security improvement, so its blast radius was not examined closely.
solution: Backfilled the missing tokens into the time-series store and changed the request router to distinguish a lookup failure from an invalid credential so the next occurrence is diagnosed faster. Validation changes are staged behind a per-tenant warning period before they are enforced.

issue: Errors on the reporting UI following a recent change.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the geocoding service. The new default disagreed with the request router, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the request router cannot parse before it reaches the shared staging-to-production path.

issue: Single sign-on to the public API failed for 3% of enterprise tenants for 14 minutes. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A clock drift of several minutes on the request router caused assertions to fall outside their validity window, and the resulting rejection was reported to users as an invalid credential.
solution: Corrected time synchronisation on the request router, added monitoring on clock drift, and made the error message distinguish a timing rejection from a bad credential. Key rotation now publishes the new key and accepts both for an overlap window before retiring the old one.

issue: Errors on the admin console following a recent change.
root_cause: A dependency upgrade removed a method the token validator still called. The build succeeded because the call sits on a path exercised only at runtime, so the failure appeared first in the production fleet. The previous configuration had been in place long enough that no one recalled why the superseded value mattered.
solution: Rolled back the upgrade, added the missing call path to the integration test suite, and enabled dependency pinning with an explicit review step for minor-version bumps.

issue: The feed builder became unavailable in ca-central following a disk failure on a node that continued reporting itself healthy.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the feed builder failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: The scheduling service ran with configuration from the previous release for 1 hour 12 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The change was written to a configuration path that the scheduling service stopped reading in an earlier refactor.
solution: Pointed the change at the configuration path the scheduling service actually reads and added a test that fails when a documented setting is not consumed by the service that owns it. Staged rollouts with an automatic health gate were introduced so a bad configuration can no longer reach the whole fleet.

issue: Internal name resolution failed across a single production cell and services could no longer reach one another for 4 hours 36 minutes.
root_cause: A DNS configuration change was deployed to the infrastructure hosting a single production cell.
solution: Rolled the DNS configuration change back to restore resolution, then extended pre-production testing to exercise the same resolution path used in production.

issue: The inventory service terminated repeatedly on memory exhaustion.
root_cause: Memory was lost to fragmentation rather than a genuine leak. An aligned-allocation pattern in the shard mapper interacted poorly with the system allocator in that environment, permanently fragmenting the pool even though every allocation was correctly freed.
solution: Replaced the aligned-allocation pattern with a dedicated allocator that avoids the fragmenting path, which stopped the steady growth under sustained load.

issue: The inventory service ran with configuration from the previous release for 14 minutes even though the deploy reported success.
root_cause: The configuration was delivered to the job scheduler but the inventory service reads its settings only at process start, and the rollout did not restart the running instances, so they continued serving with the previous values.
solution: Restarted the affected instances to pick up the new configuration, then added a post-apply check that reads the live value back from each instance before the rollout is marked complete. The affected path was added to pre-production verification so the same defect would be caught before release.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the sync service in two of three availability zones.
root_cause: Redundant power feeds into the rack hosting the sync service were found to share an upstream component.
solution: Moved the affected equipment onto genuinely independent feeds and audited the remaining racks for shared upstream components behind nominally redundant paths. Maintenance and fleet upgrades may no longer overlap in the same region without an explicit capacity check.

issue: Elevated query latency against the Kafka topic. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the Kafka topic stalled without raising an error. Monitoring tracked replica availability but not replication lag, so the stall was invisible until customers reported inconsistency. The backlog that built up during the incident took longer to drain than the original fault lasted.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness. Destructive operations now require a second approval and an explicit target allow-list.

issue: Infrastructure fault degrading the asset pipeline.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning errors for a subset of requests. The metrics agent retried aggressively without backoff, which both prolonged recovery and amplified load on the recovering dependency.
solution: Throttled retries to break the amplification loop and added exponential backoff with jitter plus a cap on concurrent calls to a third-party SMS gateway.

issue: Work assigned to one node in us-east stalled for 4 hours 36 minutes while the node remained in rotation.
root_cause: A node in us-east entered a degraded state where it accepted connections but could not complete disk operations.
solution: Removed the node from rotation and changed the probe to verify end-to-end operation rather than process liveness alone. An out-of-band access path was established so recovery does not depend on the affected infrastructure.

issue: Queries against the ledger table slowed from milliseconds to several seconds, and the feed builder began timing out for 31% of requests. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A schema migration on the ledger table was applied as a drop-then-create rather than a single modification.
solution: Recreated the index to restore query plans, then changed the migration tool to treat an index modification as one atomic operation instead of a drop followed by a create. A review step was added that rejects a new query path without an index backing its filter columns.

issue: 78% of users on the reporting UI saw an unreleased interface for 6 hours 10 minutes before it was withdrawn.
root_cause: A feature flag for the document indexer was created with a default-on value rather than default-off. The flag service treats an absent per-tenant override as the default, so every tenant without an explicit override received the new behaviour.
solution: Set the flag to default-off and re-enabled it only for the intended internal tenants, then made the flag service require an explicit default at creation time. Drift detection now alerts on any divergence between intended and applied state.

issue: A rollback intended to resolve an earlier problem with the sync service made the incident worse and extended impact by 1 hour 12 minutes. Both the partner API and internal tooling were affected.
root_cause: The forward deploy performed a one-way data change in the DynamoDB table, so the previous release could not interpret rows written after the cutover and rejected them during normal reads. Because the change was applied fleet-wide rather than in stages, every instance was affected before anyone could intervene.
solution: Deployed a reader that accepted both formats, reconciled the affected rows in the DynamoDB table, and made backward-incompatible data changes require a two-phase rollout.

issue: Capacity in ap-southeast fell by 31% and the catalogue API began shedding requests.
root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in ap-southeast below what was needed to serve normal traffic.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: 31% of users could not sign in to the mobile apps for 6 hours 10 minutes, with no clear pattern by region or account type.
root_cause: An access policy changed during a routine security review blocked a resource beyond its intended scope, which included the path the session store uses to validate credentials for the webhook dispatcher.
solution: Rolled the policy change back to its intended narrower scope, restoring sign-in, then added a pre-apply check that lists the resources a policy change will affect.

issue: Capacity reduction affecting the pricing engine in sa-east.
root_cause: A hardware failure in network equipment reduced available capacity in sa-east below what was needed to serve normal traffic. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the shortfall.
solution: Rerouted traffic manually and replaced the failed equipment, then provisioned additional headroom so a single component failure cannot push the region below serviceable capacity.

issue: The ingest gateway degraded by a datastore problem.
root_cause: The connection pool for the ingest gateway was sized for a previous instance count. After a scale-out, the combined pools exceeded what the DynamoDB table would accept and new connections were refused. Replicas fell behind as the primary absorbed the extra work, which removed read capacity exactly when it was most needed.
solution: Reduced the per-instance pool size so the fleet total stays within the server limit, and tied pool sizing to instance count rather than a fixed value. Backup success is now monitored directly, and restore drills were scheduled to verify snapshots are usable.

issue: A handful of reads served by the document indexer reflected data minutes behind the primary.
root_cause: A long-running analytical query held a lock that blocked replication apply on the Elasticsearch index, so replicas stayed available while falling progressively further behind.
solution: Terminated the blocking query, moved analytical workloads to a dedicated replica, and added a lag threshold that removes a replica from the read pool automatically.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the ingest gateway across the production fleet.
root_cause: A release changed a default in the shared configuration bundle for the ingest gateway. The new default disagreed with the request router, which rejected every request it could not map to a known setting. Nothing compared the applied state against the intended state, so the divergence persisted until customers reported it.
solution: Reverted the changed default and added a pre-apply validation step that rejects a configuration bundle the request router cannot parse before it reaches the production fleet.

issue: Authentication failures affecting the sync service.
root_cause: A signing key used by the job scheduler was rotated without updating every validator, so tokens issued after the rotation were rejected by the services still holding the previous key.
solution: Distributed the new key to all validators and changed rotation to publish the new key and accept both for an overlap window before retiring the old one. A dual-read path was added so a change to session or token format cannot invalidate everything at once.

issue: 3% of requests to the embedded widget failed while every internal component reported healthy.
root_cause: An upstream payment processor experienced a regional fault. The notification service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available. Nothing reconciled the output against its source, so the discrepancy persisted until a customer raised it.
solution: Served a reduced experience while an upstream payment processor recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The webhooks endpoint began returning errors for 7% of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the document indexer itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the document indexer started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the document indexer within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: Request throughput on the SQLite metadata store rose steadily over 38 minutes and the billing service began shedding requests, with no change in traffic volume. A subset of tenants saw no impact at all.
root_cause: An index on the devices table concentrated a frequently-read key range onto a small number of shards in the SQLite metadata store. A short cache expiry forced frequent refreshes, so read contention on those shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose. The additional load pushed the cluster past the point where it could serve its normal read volume, so unrelated queries also began failing.
solution: Redistributed the hot key range across more shards and lengthened the cache expiry to cut refresh frequency, which brought read contention back to normal. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: Database errors affecting the geocoding service.
root_cause: The final rename step of the migration took a lock that conflicted with ongoing reads on a large share of the replicas in the MySQL replica set.
solution: Recovered the affected replicas and restored capacity, then changed the final migration step to swap a prepared table rather than take a conflicting lock.

issue: Unexpected behaviour in the identity service across the shared staging-to-production path.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the identity service did not set, so the health checker silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the health checker to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Read and write errors against the object store bucket.
root_cause: Replication from the primary to the read replicas in the object store bucket stalled without raising an error. Monitoring tracked replica availability but not replication lag, so the stall was invisible until customers reported inconsistency.
solution: Restarted replication to clear the stall and added an explicit lag metric with alerting, rather than treating replica availability as a proxy for freshness.

issue: The feed builder unavailable following a planned change.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the feed builder did not set, so the job scheduler silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the job scheduler to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Latency on the web dashboard crept upward across the day with no corresponding rise in traffic.
root_cause: A cache in front of the DynamoDB table was configured with an expiry short enough that most reads missed.
solution: Lengthened the cache expiry to a value matched to how often the underlying data actually changes, which raised the hit rate and returned latency to normal.

issue: Unplanned disruption affecting the sync service. Internal tooling was affected alongside customer-facing traffic.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway began returning malformed responses rather than errors. The admission controller had no validation on the response shape, so it propagated the bad data as a failure further downstream.
solution: Added response validation in the admission controller so a malformed upstream reply is rejected at the boundary, and raised an explicit alert distinguishing an upstream fault from an internal one.

issue: The recommendation service could not create new records, returning a database-level error unrelated to any application change.
root_cause: A foreign key column on the events table was declared with a narrower integer type than the primary key it referenced.
solution: Widened the foreign key column to match the referenced key and added a schema check that compares column types across a reference before a migration is accepted. Migrations touching a large relation now run against a single replica first, with a gate before fleet-wide application.

issue: 85% of requests to the admin console failed while every internal component reported healthy. Impact was limited to the Frankfurt region.
root_cause: A third-party SMS gateway experienced a regional fault. The checkout service depends on it for a step it cannot complete locally, so the upstream problem surfaced directly to customers with no degraded mode available.
solution: Served a reduced experience while a third-party SMS gateway recovered, then added a cached fallback and a status banner so an upstream fault degrades rather than removes the feature.

issue: The partner API slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: A single tenant sent a concentrated burst that saturated a shared worker pool. Nothing isolated tenants from one another, so the burst degraded the geocoding service for every caller.
solution: Introduced per-tenant concurrency limits so one caller's burst cannot consume the shared pool, and added autoscaling keyed on queue depth.

issue: Requests to the identity service failed across the shared staging-to-production path immediately following a scheduled configuration rollout. The problem resolved and recurred twice before being fully mitigated.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the shared staging-to-production path because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the identity service started with settings it could not validate.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the identity service within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying. A pre-apply diff review was added that reports the runtime effect of a change rather than only its text.

issue: The webhooks endpoint began returning errors for a handful of requests minutes after a routine deploy, with no code change to the webhook dispatcher itself.
root_cause: A configuration change intended for one environment was applied to the production fleet because the rollout tooling resolved the target by name prefix rather than exact match, so the webhook dispatcher started with settings it could not validate. Alerting fired on the symptom rather than the change, so the connection to the rollout was not made immediately.
solution: Rolled the configuration bundle back to the previous known-good revision, which restored the webhook dispatcher within minutes, then changed the rollout tooling to require an exact environment match before applying.

issue: The inventory service degraded by a platform-level failure.
root_cause: A disk on a node hosting the inventory service failed in a way that prevented writes while the node continued to pass its health probe, so the orchestrator left it in service and kept scheduling work that could not complete. Automated failover moved some load but could not compensate for the size of the capacity shortfall.
solution: Drained and replaced the failed node, then extended the health probe to exercise a real write so a node that cannot do useful work is removed automatically.

issue: Elevated error rates after a release to production.
root_cause: An admission policy added earlier in the week required a label that the deployment template for the geocoding service did not set, so the config loader silently rejected every new instance.
solution: Added the required label to the deployment template and changed the config loader to surface rejected instances as a deploy failure instead of leaving them pending without an alert.

issue: Reverting a deploy of the feed builder did not restore service and left the Cassandra ring in a state neither version could read.
root_cause: The deploy had already written records to the Cassandra ring in a new format. Rolling the code back left the older version reading rows it had no schema for, so the feed builder failed on a larger share of requests than before the rollback. Impact was uniform across tenants, which initially pointed responders towards a dependency rather than a local change.
solution: Rolled forward to a build that tolerated both record formats, backfilled the affected rows, and added a rule that a deploy touching a stored format must ship its reader before its writer.
